LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. The defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks are coming off a loss at home to the San Francisco 49ers, dropping them to two games back of first place in the NFC West. Seattle has struggled a bit on offense, as Sam Darnold has not looked as sharp as he did last season. Darnold had a glute injury in Week 1 that sidelined him for a game, but he has started three games in a row for Seattle, leading it to a 1-2 record. Seattle still remains an elite defensive team, ranking No. 1 in the league in yards per play allowed and EPA/Play this season. The Denver defense (11th in EPA/Play and success rate) is off to a strong start as well, but the offense has lagged behind. Bo Nix is really struggling in his third NFL season, and Denver is averaging the seventh-fewest yards per play (4.7) in the NFL. Denver and Seattle both have playoff expectations – and Super Bowl hopes – in the 2026 season, but their offenses have to improve to make those dreams a reality. With Denver banged up a bit in the secondary on Thursday, Seattle has a shot to get back on track. It won’t be easy, though, as the Broncos are 2-0 at home with impressive victories against Jacksonville and the Los Angeles Rams. All week long, the SI Betting team has shared game picks, player props, anytime touchdown scorer picks and more for this primetime matchup. Denver's defensive numbers are that good while having played some of the best offenses in the league to begin the season, including the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, and 49ers, so expect them to improve their standing in their defensive analytics soon. Meanwhile, I have some question marks about both offenses. They rank 24th and 26th in EPA per play, and Seattle's offense is in a tough spot, having to play at altitude in Denver on a short week. This total is a touch too high, I'll bet the UNDER. Overall, the star wideout has been targeted 50 times by Seattle’s quarterbacks, reeling in 37 passes for 583 yards and seven scores. He should see a bunch of targets in Week 6 against a Denver secondary that is dealing with a bunch of injuries early in the season. The Broncos are fifth in the NFL in EPA/Pass, but Sam Darnold has locked in on JSN all season long, so I don’t expect his target share to waver. He’s found the end zone in back-to-back games, registering two rushing scores and one receiving score. Denver has struggled against the run in 2026, allowing 4.7 yards per carry and five rushing touchdowns in five games. I think the ground game may be the easier way for Seattle to beat this Denver defense, so I like Wilson at +125 since he’s monopolized carries in recent weeks. The defending World Champion Seattle Seahawks are coming to Mile High for a Thursday Night Football throwdown. It's a short-week turnaround for both teams, with the Broncos coming off a win and the Seahawks off a loss. Broncos-Seahawks was the Super Bowl many people expected last season before Bo Nix's shocking ankle injury. When the 2026 schedule dropped earlier this year, this game was circled as a potential Super Bowl preview. Despite both teams sitting at 3-2, few people currently view the Broncos as a true Super Bowl contender, but that's no different than the general consensus at this time last year. The narrative around the Seahawks, though, is strikingly different. What's the disconnect? Offense. The Broncos' offense and the quality of quarterback play haven't been at a Super Bowl level — but the season is still young. How will Broncos-Seahawks shake out on Thursday night? We're going around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff foresee this one playing out at Mile High. You can connect with each staff on X (their handles are linked next to their names). Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 4-1 : Another week where the Broncos decided to take the first three quarters off before finally showing up. At some point, it gets a little anticlimactic. away.headline: Seahawks injury report; DT Leonard Williams good to go for NFL Week 5
away.blurb: Some good news for the Seahawks, especially on the injury front. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams carries no game time designation, which means he is good to go for Sunday. Williams was limited on Wednesday, and did not practice Thursday due to his ankle. However, it truly does appear his ankle wasn't serious, as Mike Macdonald alluded to earlier in the week. There is some bad news, however. Cornerback Julian Neal and linebacker Chazz Surratt have been ruled OUT for Sunday. Additionally, running back Zach Charbonnet is also OUT, but that's not really a surprise at this point. Running back George Holani and wide receiver Irv Charles are QUESTIONABLE. If Holani is not able to go, expect heavy dosage of Emanuel Wilson and Velus Jones Jr. Don't be surprised if we see Rashid Shaheed back in action in the backfield against the 49ers. home.headline: Seahawks’ Week 6 injury report vs. Broncos: Will Jaxon Smith-Njigba play after suffering ankle injury?
home.blurb: Let's look at the Seahawks' injury report for Week 6 and see who will be ruled out for Seattle. RB Zach Charbonnet – OUT (knee) LB Chazz Surratt – OUT (calf) LB Drake Thomas – OUT (ankle) Let's start with bad news first. The most notable omission from the roster is linebacker Drake Thomas. Thomas, who has played in 86% of all defensive snaps this season, has been ruled out after suffering an ankle injury. He's a starter for one of the best defenses in the league, so his absence will be sorely missed by the Seahawks. The good news for Seattle is that Smith-Njigba is absent from the injury report. The reigning Offensive Player of the Year was a limited participant on Monday and Tuesday, but was a full participant yesterday. The Seahawks wide receiver will also have an easier time against the Broncos, as former DPOY Pat Surtain was also ruled out. Other notable limited participants during the lead-up to Week 6 include DT Leonard Williams, QB Drew Lock, and backup RB George Holani. All three players do not carry an injury designation in the game against the Broncos. Aside from Surtain, the Broncos won't have Talanoa Hufanga available to take on the Seahawks. Cornerback Riley Moss is listed as questionable as well. But the numbers beneath those records leave room for a considerably less predictable afternoon in London. Jacksonville enters as a 2.5-point favorite after escaping Philadelphia 19-17. Houston finally broke through by beating Tennessee 26-3, then acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. These predictions deliberately push beyond a narrow upset or another respectable quarterback performance. The forecast: Houston produces its most complete game of the season. CJ Stroud throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Jacksonville's defense allows only 14 points per game, second in the NFL. Predicting four passing touchdowns against that unit is aggressive, but its strength against the run can obscure a vulnerable pass defense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Jaguars surrender 277.2 passing yards per game, ranking 30th. Conversely, they allow an NFL-best 63.8 rushing yards per game and just 2.9 yards per carry. Houston therefore has good reason to attack through Stroud rather than repeatedly challenge Jacksonville's strongest area. Stroud has already thrown for 1,402 yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions through five games. Against Tennessee, he completed 26 of 34 attempts for 261 yards, including an impressive eight completions on 11 pressured throws for 115 yards. The prediction requires Houston to convert passing volume into touchdowns, something it has not consistently accomplished. Harrison's arrival creates another possible weapon, although his debut and workload remain uncertain. This call rests primarily on Stroud's existing production and Jacksonville's passing-yardage vulnerability, not an assumption that the newcomer immediately dominates. Will Anderson Jr. records four sacks as Houston forces three turnovers Anderson delivered three of Houston's four sacks against Tennessee, providing the foundation for an even bigger prediction against Jacksonville. Four sacks by one player would be a spectacular follow-up, not merely continued improvement. The Texans limited the Titans to 187 total yards and three points after DeMeco Ryans reclaimed defensive play-calling duties. Tennessee's struggling offense makes that result an imperfect measuring stick, but Houston still ranks ninth in yards allowed per play. Jacksonville presents a tougher opponent, yet Sunday exposed pressure points. Trevor Lawrence threw an interception and lost a fumble against Philadelphia despite producing 331 passing yards and two touchdowns. Houston must turn disruptive plays into possession changes, rather than simply allowing Jacksonville to reset after sacks. The Jaguars' penalty problems could help create those opportunities. They have committed at least 13 penalties and accumulated more than 100 penalty yards in consecutive games. Backward movement makes passing situations more predictable, giving Anderson additional chances to attack. The bold call is four Anderson sacks and three Houston takeaways: pressure converts Jacksonville's mistakes into decisive field-position advantages. The Texans win by at least 17 points Jacksonville's winning record and scoring defense make a comfortable Houston victory the biggest leap here. The Jaguars have allowed only 70 points across five games, while the Texans entered last Sunday without a win. Nevertheless, a blowout becomes plausible if the first two predictions connect. Houston's passing offense attacks Jacksonville's statistical weakness, while turnovers supply short fields and prevent Lawrence from answering every score. Jacksonville also needed a 53-yard kickoff return and Cam Little's 57-yard field goal to escape Philadelphia. That extraordinary finish demonstrated resilience, but it should not conceal how close the Jaguars came to losing. Stroud's four touchdown passes power the offense, and defensive disruption keeps the Jaguars from turning their rushing balance into sustained control. London delivers a division-changing upset, not another last-second escape. Jacksonville enters the game at 4-1 after a dramatic 17-16 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, sealed by Cam Little's 57 yard field goal in the final seconds. Houston is 1-4 but comes into the matchup with renewed confidence after earning its first win of the season, a convincing 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans. Kickoff is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET at Wembley Stadium, with coverage on NFL Network. C.J. Stroud Leads Houston's Offense Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud will be a key player to watch as Houston looks to continue its turnaround. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a touchdown against Tennessee, spreading the ball around to seven different receivers. His ability to distribute the football and make plays downfield will be important against a Jacksonville defense that has helped the Jaguars get off to a strong start. Houston also recently added wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with Arizona. Harrison reunites with Stroud after their time together at Ohio State, giving the Texans another potential weapon in the passing game. Head coach DeMeco Ryans will also want his defense to maintain the intensity it showed against Tennessee. Houston limited the Titans to just three points and 187 total yards, providing an encouraging sign after a difficult opening month. Head coach Liam Coen has Jacksonville playing competitive football, and the team's ability to find ways to win close games has been important during its early-season success. The Jaguars will look to establish their offense and take advantage of opportunities against Houston. However, Jacksonville must also adjust along the offensive line after left tackle Anton Harrison suffered a knee injury against Philadelphia. Walker Little is expected to step into the starting role, creating an important challenge against Houston's pass rush. An Important AFC South Battle Sunday's matchup gives Houston an opportunity to build on its first victory and make progress within the division. Jacksonville, meanwhile, can continue its strong start and maintain its position near the top of the AFC South. With Stroud looking to keep Houston's offense moving and Lawrence leading a Jacksonville team that has found ways to win, the London matchup offers an important test for both sides.

The Texans are coming off their first win while the Jags take the field following their most unlikely win of the season. A preseason favorite of many to contend for the Super Bowl, Houston finally got into the win column last week with an impressive 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville. For the first time this season, the highly touted Texans dominated defensively, limiting Tennessee to just three points and 187 Total Yards. C.J. Stroud connected on passes to seven different receivers and threw for 261 yards to lead the attack on offense. Jacksonville, meanwhile, won a game they may not have deserved but were glad to have been gifted. They knocked off the Eagles, 19-17, at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Philadelphia took the lead with eight seconds remaining. Jacksonville was without a timeout, but Ameer Abdullah managed to return the ensuing kickoff 53 yards in seven seconds. Cam Little then converted a 57-yard field goal as time expired to win the game for the Jags. Jacksonville has now won three straight. They lead the AFC South by two games over the Colts and three games over the Texans. Stroud and the Texans have moved the ball through the air (No. 4 in the NFL with 1402 yards), but only Green Bay has gained fewer yards on the ground (No. 31 with 395 yards). Couple that disparity with an issue turning yardage into points – they have scored as a team just 11 touchdowns this season – and the 1-4 start is not all that surprising. Jacksonville’s fast start is based on the defensive side of the ball. The Jags allow yards but not points. They are the No. 2 scoring defense in the league allowing just 70 points through five games. Bottom line: Was last week’s win the start of a turnaround for Houston or will Jacksonville build on the good fortune they received last week and for all intents and purposes end the Texans’ hopes in the division? home.headline: Jaguars turn to Jacob Bobenmoyer after Ross Matiscik injury: Report
home.blurb: NFL MLB NBA NHL NCAA Football NCAA Basketball UFC/MMA PGA Tour Games JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS Jaguars sign Jacob Bobenmoyer to practice squad after Matiscik injury Jacob Bobenmoyer will take over snapping duties after DaVon Hamilton's emergency stint, per report. This story was updated to add new information. The Jacksonville Jaguars have found a replacement for defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton , who served as the team's long snapper for most of Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles in London. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday that the long snapper was arriving shortly, and he's now at The Grove with the rest of the team. According to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport, the Jaguars will sign veteran long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer , while typical starting long snapper Ross Matiscik recovers from a shoulder injury sustained in the first quarter against Philly. Who is long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer, Ross Matiscik's replacement? Bobenmoyer, 29, has spent seven years in the NFL with two teams: the Denver Broncos (2019-2022) and the Las Vegas Raiders (2023-2025). Bobenmoyer has played 97 games, recording 22 tackles and 1 fumble recovery. Jacksonville is currently overseas in London as it prepares to play its second of two matchups across the pond. The Jaguars will take on the Houston Texans in Week 6. According to Rapoport, Bobenmoyer has already flown to London. Hamilton stepped in for Jacksonville after Matiscik was injured. Teams typically carry only one long snapper on their 53-man roster or practice squad. Sunday's win marked the second time Hamilton served as the team's long snapper after Matiscik's injury. Hamilton helped set up Cam Little 's game-winning 57-yard field goal . Although Hamilton's snap was high, punter Logan Cooke got the ball down quickly, giving Little time to boot it through the uprights. The Jaguars won in the final seconds against the Eagles, 19-17. The Jaguars (4-1) will face off against the Texans in Week 6 at Wembley Stadium as they look to bury their division rival. The Texans are currently 1-4 after netting their first win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. Demetrius Harvey is the Jacksonville Jaguars reporter for the Florida Times-Union. Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has missed each of the team's last three games since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season. away.blurb: Injury Update: Bears RB Kyle Monangai ruled out, QB Caleb Williams questionable for Packers game Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Molly Kaiser/Chicago Bears Bears running back Kyle Monangai has been ruled out of Sunday's game in Green Bay with a toe injury he sustained in last weekend's 23-12 win over the Jets. "We were certainly conscious of the thumb, and it turns out the toe is a bigger deal than we initially anticipated," said coach Ben Johnson, who described Monangai's status as week-to-week. "We've got him with a specialist and so we'll work through that. He's in a boot currently and we'll go from there." Running back D'Andre Swift was a full participant in Friday's practice and was not given an injury designation for Sunday's game after sitting out Wednesday and being limited Thursday with hip and knee issues. With Monangai out, fourth-year running back Roschon Johnson moves up a spot to No. 2 on the depth chart. The 6-foot, 227-pounder has rushed for 16 yards on four carries this year—all in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's win over the Jets. "Bigger body than the other guys in that room, and so I think he's a complete back. He can run hard in between the tackles. I think he's got enough speed to get to the perimeter. He catches the ball well out of the backfield and then because of his size, I think he's an asset in pass protection as well. So, he can do a little bit of everything, which we really value at that spot." Quarterback Caleb Williams, meanwhile, returned to practice on a limited basis Friday for the first time since injuring his hamstring in the fourth quarter of a Week 2 game against the Vikings. He is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest, though Johnson announced Monday that Tyson Bagent will start in Green Bay. home.blurb: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has not played since Week 2 with a Grade 2 hamstring strain, but he was listed as questionable for Week 5 against the Green Bay Packers before sitting out. Now, it appears Williams is on track to play in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons, even though there have been conflicting reports about his health over the last week. NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported on Monday that "all signs" point to the former No. 1 overall pick making his return on Sunday. Chicago's first practice report will come out on Wednesday, and if Williams is limited or a full participant, it will bode well for his chances of playing in Week 6. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. Obviously, the buck stops with the head coach, but why did offensive coordinator David Blough call a play that USED MOTION as precious seconds ticked off the clock, and how was quarterback Jayd

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson is “day-to-day” with the ankle injury that he suffered in Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans. Jackson did not play in the Ravens’ win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5, as Tyler Huntley (three total scores) led Baltimore to a victory – their third straight with him in the lineup for an injured Jackson dating back to the 2025 season. Minter said that Lamar Jackson remains “day to day” and when he’s ready, he’ll be out at practice. There has been a ton of movement in the odds for this game between the Ravens and Browns, as oddsmakers are gauging whether or not the two-time league MVP will play. Sports Illustrated spoke with several oddsmakers to give bettors some insight into how the spread for this game is currently set, and where it could move if Jackson doesn’t play. “The line this week indicates Jackson is around 60/40 to go and a revision will be made one way or the other once we know more on his status,” Johnny Avello, Director of Race and Sports Operations for DraftKings Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. “There were no adjustments made with the Ravens winning on Sunday night, since backups don’t usually play as well in back-to-back games as opponents have more time to prepare.” After the Ravens opened as 3.5-point favorites against the Browns on Sunday night, that line has moved quite a bit toward Baltimore. The Ravens were 4.5-point favorites early in the week and moved as far as 5.5-point favorites at home books after ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday that Jackson had a “realistic” chance to play against Cleveland. However, the star quarterback then missed practice, causing some books to adjust the line towards the Browns. “We're sitting at five on our site,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated on Wednesday. “As it currently stands as of this moment, and as Lamar's status becomes murkier, that will likely go further towards the Browns.” Still, the opening number that books shared baked in an expectation for the two-time MVP to play. Jackson’s injury isn’t considered to be a long-term issue, and he’s been one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL when he’s been able to take the field in 2026. In his four games in the 2026 campaign, Jackson has completed 70.8 percent of his passes in 2026 for 967 yards, six scores and one pick while adding 18 carries for 144 yards and a score on the ground. "Looking at this line, we are expecting Lamar to play," Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated . "It will drop to under three if Lamar ends up being out. No change for Baltimore, Snoop (Huntley) is a capable backup who has similar strengths to Lamar. They do not need to change their offense when Lamar is out, which is very helpful." While BetMGM has priced Sunday’s game with the expectation that Jackson will be in the lineup, not every book has done so. FanDuel considers Jackson “questionable” in Week 6, yet it still has the Ravens as 5.5-point favorites on Thursday. “We are pricing the Browns Ravens game as if Lamar is truly questionable to play,” a FanDuel trader told Sports Illustrated. “If he is announced in/out the line will move to or away from the Ravens based on his status. Tyler Huntley's performance last week may affect this week's matchup with the Browns, but it will not change the outlook on Baltimore as a whole as their ceiling and range of outcomes is firmly tied to Lamar Jackson's health." Thursday’s practice for Baltimore will likely impact this line, as another DNP from Jackson would be a concerning sign for his chances of playing on Sunday. The Ravens are still capable of winning games with Huntley, who has completed 78.0 percent of his passes for 264 yards and two scores in 1.5 games this season. He’s also carried the ball 10 times for 36 yards and a score. Bettors that want to take the Ravens may want to wait for a more concrete update around Jackson’s status, as it seems pretty clear the betting market has set the spread for this game with the expectation that he’s more likely to play than not. picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 2:04 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns are coming off their first loss since Week 1 as they head into Week 6. They are now 3-2 and have a pivotal matchup with the Baltimore Ravens on the horizon in what has now become a must-win game for them. The Browns can only control what they can control, and in Week 6 that is going to be more important than ever. The Ravens have been dealing with several injuries, including the most notable one regarding Lamar Jackson. Whether he plays or not, this defense needs to prepare the way they know how to. On offense, Todd Monken and Deshaun Watson have to find that spark again after losing the momentum they had been building. Without doing both of those things, this could be a major setback for the season as a whole. With that said, we have our eyes on three matchups within this game that we want to highlight. Carson Schwesinger vs. Lamar Jackson Carson Schwesinger has played at an All-Pro level this year, but he is dealing with an ankle injury. Also dealing with an ankle injury is Lamar Jackson. Neither man is likely to be 100%, so who will have the willpower to overcome the other? Schwesinger has been really flashing his pass-rush presence in 2026, which will help contain Lamar Jackson, but he also has just done a tremendous job patrolling the middle of the field. He will have to be on his A game against one of the best players of this generation. Denzel Ward vs. Zay Flowers Denzel Ward is quietly having one of the best seasons of his career, just as Zay Flowers is. The Browns cornerback has allowed an average of just 20 yards to players he is covering in 2026. On the flip side, Zay Flowers is averaging 97.3 yards per game, something has to give, right? Flowers has been pretty well contained in his career against the Browns, but every matchup is a fresh start. Whoever wins this matchup between two proverbial titans could tip the scales in their team's favor. Todd Monken vs. Jessee Minter Todd Monken will be playing against the team he left to become a head coach this offseason. He is familiar with the Ravens, Lamar Jackson, Zay Flowers, and everyone on that offense, so what will he be able to do to help Mike Rutenberg and his defense? On the flip side, Jesse Minter is looking to continue the hot start to his coaching career as the Ravens themselves are sitting pretty at 4-1. These coaches seem poised to face each other for years, but the first matchup will perhaps be the most interesting. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Ravens Injury Report: Lamar Jackson Out, Zay Flowers Questionable
away.blurb: Ravens Injury Report: Lamar Jackson Out, Zay Flowers Questionable - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens Injury Report: Lamar Jackson Out, Zay Flowers Questionable Head coach Jesse Minter ruled out quarterback Lamar Jackson due to his sprained ankle , but Jackson isn't the only concern on the final report. As stated, Jackson is out after suffering a sprained ankle in Week 4. Instead of getting him back on the field, which could cause more damage, Minter chose to sit the starter. There are more concerns on the injury report, other than Jackson. Wide receiver Zay Flowers is also questionable due to his foot injury. Flowers was limited all week, but he has toughed out injuries before. The nagging hamstring injury that he had led him to being limited in previous weeks but he still managed to only miss one game. Should Flowers be out, this would be a huge loss for the Ravens' offense, especially with Huntley behind center. Right guard Andrew Vorhees is also questionable. He suffered a foot injury in Week 4 and was limited on two of the three practice days leading up to the Falcons matchup. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey is also questionable due to a calf and hamstring injury. He has been limited and missed Wednesday's practice. Should he not be healthy enough to play, it will be Chidobe Awuzie taking over. Outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson also remains out due to the procedure he underwent to fix his broken finger. Minter indicated that it would not keep him out long-term, but the pass rusher has now missed the past two games. There are no other major concerns on the injury report, and the Ravens' inactives will be what reveals the fate of the other questionable players that were listed above. If Vorhees cannot play, it will be Emory Jones Jr. stepping in at center, as Cam Jurgens is not ready. Jurgens is expected to take over as center, leading to rookie Vega Ioane being kicked back to right guard. Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. Gilberto Manzano correctly bet on the Green Bay Packers to upset the Chicago Bears, and yours truly bet on the San Francisco 49ers to beat the Seattle Seahawks. We move on to the Week 6 slate, and three writers have their upset picks locked in. Let's dive into them. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 6 Upset Pick Houston Texans (+120) vs. Jacksonville Jaguars First, let me pat myself on the back for finally getting an upset pick correctly. Now that I’ve regained your trust after my Packers-over-Bears pick came to fruition last week, do yourself a favor and take the new-look Texans over the London Jaguars. Houston gained confidence from beating up on Tennessee and landing wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with Arizona. C.J. Stroud tends to play at his best when Nico Collins is on the field, but now he doesn’t have to lock in on him with the arrival of Harrison, who played with Stroud at Ohio State. More importantly, the Texans’ defense is back on track, and that could present trouble for the inconsistent Trevor Lawrence. Iain MacMillan Week 6 Upset Pick Tennessee Titans (+260) vs. Indianapolis Colts It's time for the Titans to get their first win of the season. You might be surprised to find out how many metrics these two teams rank similarly in, even some that the Titans outrank the Colts in, like net yards per play, which has the Titans at -0.7 and the Colts second-last in the NFL at -1.6. Another interesting metric for this game is that the Titans have the second-highest run frequency in neutral game states, meaning on early downs in the middle of the game when they still have a more than 20% win probability, Tennessee loves to run the football. That could be an area they exploit in this game, as the Colts rank dead last in the NFL in opponent rush EPA and 30th in opponent run success rate. Meanwhile, the Titans rank 16th and 11th in those two run defense categories, which will go a long way in slowing down Jonathan Taylor, which is the key to beating this Colts team. I'll take Tennessee as my upset pick of the week. Peter Dewey Week 6 Upset Pick Carolina Panthers (-105) vs. Philadelphia Eagles This isn’t the craziest upset pick in Week 6 – Carolina is just a 1.5-point underdog – but I can’t pass up a chance to fade this Philadelphia offense. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are dealing with soft-tissue injuries, and the Eagles currently rank 30th in EPA/Play, 31st in success rate and 31st in yards per play this season. Only the Tennessee Titans (0-5) are averaging fewer yards per play than Philly. I think there’s a real chance that Bryce Young and this Carolina offense (eighth in EPA/Play, sixth in EPA/Pass and fifth in yards per play) put up too many points for this Eagles team to compete. After all, the Eagles are 17th in yards per play allowed on defense and 22nd in both EPA/Play and success rate. Both of those advanced numbers are behind the Panthers’ defense this season. If the Eagles didn’t enter the season with playoff expectations, I think they’d be underdogs on Sunday based on their statistical profile in 2026. Plus, Carolina is coming off a bye while the Eagles have a tough travel week coming from London. All signs point to a Panthers upset in Week 6. That's not an overreaction, but more a growing possibility after Tennessee laid out a laundry list of struggles in its 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans on Oct. 11. Now, the Titans (0-5, 0-1 AFC South) are a seven-point underdog before its divisional road game against the Indianapolis Colts (2-3, 1-0) at Lucas Oil Stadium on Oct. 18 (noon CT, FOX). The Colts are one of four teams with losing records remaining on the Titans' schedule. It doesn't seem right to circle those games as easy opportunities for coach Robert Saleh, considering the Texans were 0-4 when they blitzed the Titans. Quarterback Cam Ward and Tennessee's best chances will be against sub-.500 teams. But even that has been a struggle in a weak AFC South. Nas 0728 Titans Camp 003 | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Jon Spradley Mon, October 12, 2026 at 11:01 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Indianapolis Colts are picking up divisional play in Week 6 against the Tennessee Titans. It's a welcomed return home after a road trip that produced mixed results. After traveling to London and collecting a win, things went sideways in Pittsburgh. FanDuel Sportsbook is giving the Colts the edge against the winless Titans with a 6.5-point spread advantage. The money line is at -330 with the over/under starting at 43.5. The Colts did what they do; they lost in Pittsburgh. Unable to finish drives and giving up huge plays on defense was the story of the afternoon. After going up 3-0, they never regained the lead. Every time the Colts got close, they had to settle for 3. Luckily, Spencer Schrader was on his game, but it wasn't enough. An 80 and 50 yard score by Jaylen Warren was too much to overcome as the Colts fell, once again, to the Steelers in Pittsburgh. The Titans and Texans were entrenched in the battle of the winless as one team would get off the schneid and the other would sink further down. Cam Ward and the Titans might really be that bad. They scored the first 3 but then allowed the Texans to rattle off the next 26. Jobs might be on the line as the season is quickly slipping down the drain. Lose again and the Titans might be eyeing a replacement for Ward in the draft with the No. 1 pick. The Colts have work to do, but the Titans might be the best remedy to what ails them. Nothing is certain, but this is a great opportunity to get to 3-3 and finish the first third of the season at .500. Finding the end zone and putting up 6 in place of 3 is a great place to start. The Colts can do it, but they have plenty to tighten up before then.

Tennessee enters Week 6 at 0-5 after suffering a disappointing 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans. Indianapolis is 2-3 following a 34-22 defeat against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Both teams are looking to respond, but the Titans desperately need their first victory of the season. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Cam Ward Looks to Spark Tennessee's Offense Titans quarterback Cam Ward remains the centerpiece of Tennessee's rebuilding effort. Despite the team's winless start, head coach Robert Saleh has continued to express confidence in the young quarterback and his ability to develop. Ward has completed 63.2% of his passes for 896 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions through five games. However, the Titans have struggled to generate consistent offense, scoring just three points against Houston last week. Tennessee needs Ward to make quicker decisions, protect the football and find ways to connect with his receivers downfield. Running back Tony Pollard will also be important. Establishing a productive ground game could take pressure off Ward and help Tennessee control possession against Indianapolis. Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor Lead Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones will look to guide Indianapolis back into the win column after the loss to Pittsburgh. Jones has thrown for 1,021 yards and three touchdowns this season, although four interceptions have contributed to some of the team's offensive inconsistency. Against Tennessee, protecting the football and taking advantage of scoring opportunities will be essential. The Colts also have one of the league's most dangerous running backs in Jonathan Taylor . Taylor has recorded 398 rushing yards and six touchdowns through five games, giving Indianapolis a reliable option to control the tempo. Wide receiver Josh Downs and tight end Tyler Warren provide Jones with additional receiving threats. Head coach Shane Steichen will look to create a balanced offensive attack that allows Taylor to establish the run while opening opportunities for Jones through the air. If Tennessee allows the Colts to establish their rushing attack early, Ward could face additional pressure to produce points quickly. Indianapolis, meanwhile, will try to pressure Ward into difficult decisions and capitalize on turnovers. A Crucial AFC South Battle Sunday presents an important opportunity for both teams. Tennessee is searching for its first win, while Indianapolis needs a response after consecutive losses. The Titans will need a more productive offensive performance from Ward, while the Colts will look to Taylor and Jones to lead the way. With both teams eager to get back on track, execution and ball security could determine the outcome of this divisional matchup.

home.headline: Two Colts starters being evaluated for concussions after Wednesday's practice
home.blurb: Right guard Matt Goncalves and defensive end Jaylahn Tuimoloau were both listed as questionable due to concussion evaluations. The two players were also both listed as limited in practice and they were not wearing red non-contact jerseys during the portion of practice open to the media on Wednesday. Tuimoloau plays a defensive end position that has already been hit hard by injury. Veteran starter Arden Key is out due to a hamstring injury, and fellow free-agent pickup Micheal Clemons is on injured reserve due to a toe injury suffered in Kansas City. With those two out, Tuimoloau played a career-high 49 snaps in Pittsburgh on Sunday, only one fewer snap than fellow starter Laiatu Latu. Daniel Jones, the team’s starting quarterback, was listed as a full participant due to an ankle injury, the first time that designation has appeared this season. Indianapolis also listed slot receiver Josh Downs as limited due to both rest and a hamstring injury. INDIANAPOLIS — The Sunday status of two Colts starters appears to be in jeopardy after the release of the team’s Wednesday injury report. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. If either Goncalves or Tuimolaou are diagnosed with concussions, they will likely miss Sunday’s game against the Titans. Under the NFL’s concussion protocol, a player must complete five steps before returning to play, and there does not appear to be enough time to complete those five steps before Sunday. An injury to Tuimoloau would likely cause larger problems. Goncalves has been playing well at right guard, but the rest of the Colts offensive line is healthy, and Indianapolis has fourth-round pick Jalen Farmer waiting in the wings in case of injury. Rookies George Gumbs Jr. (11 snaps) and Caden Curry (9) were the only other defensive ends who played against the Steelers. Indianapolis signed veteran Carl Lawson to the practice squad last week, but he has not played. Tuimolaou and Goncalves are not the only concerns on Wednesday’s injury report. The Dallas Cowboys entered Thursday night’s showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as 9.5-point favorites, yet they lost outright at home, destroying plenty of Survivor entries in the process. Week 5 had three teams that were obvious Survivor selections: Dallas, Houston and Cincinnati. They were all playing 0-4 teams, but only the Bengals and Texans came through. Luckily for the SI Betting team, neither of our editors selected the Cowboys this week, meaning that if you tailed our picks , you’re still alive heading into Week 6. Bye weeks are really starting to come into play in Survivor, as the Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, Miami Dolphins and Bengals all won’t play in Week 6. One of the best strategies in Survivor this season has been fading the 0-5 Dolphins, so players will have to look elsewhere on Sunday. There are still some huge favorites in Week 6, the Los Angeles Rams are favored by double digits at home against the Arizona Cardinals, and the Kansas City Chiefs, Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots are all favored by at least a touchdown at home. Each week, the SI Betting team of Iain MacMillan and Peter Dewey makes their favorite Survivor selections each week to help guide our readers through the season. Here’s a recap of our Week 5 selections before we dive into our favorite Survivor teams in Week 6. NFL Week 5 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Houston Texans (W) Both Dewey and MacMillan faded winless teams in Week 5, and both wins were relatively sweat free with the Texans blowing out Tennessee and Cincy cruising to a big lead in a seven-point win over Miami. There are still plenty of playoff contenders that we can choose from in Week 6, even in just a 14-game slate. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 6 Survivor Pool Picks Indianapolis Colts Indianapolis is going to be a popular pick in Survivor this week because it’s playing the Titans, but I’m willing to take a shot on Daniel Jones and company to get back to .500 at 3-3, especially at home. Indy is currently a seven-point favorite against the worst team in the AFC South. Cam Ward and the Titans have been downright awful on offense, ranking dead last in yards per play, 31st in EPA/Play and 26th in success rate during their 0-5 start. They’ve scored 20 or fewer points in every game, including three games where they scored 10 or less points. Indianapolis hasn’t done a great job of finishing drives this season, but it has one of the best kickers in the NFL in Spencer Shrader. So, Indy is able to get enough points on the board (like it did in Week 5) even if it doesn’t score a bunch of touchdowns. The Colts are allowing the third-most yards per play in the NFL on defense, which is a concern for them when it comes to this pick. However, Tennessee is 2-8 on the road in the Ward era, and it has covered the spread in just four of those games. The Indy offense isn’t a juggernaut, but it has moved the ball a lot better than the Titans, hanging 30 points on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2 while ranking 21st in success rate and 22nd in EPA/Play. I don’t see many spots where I’d willingly take the Colts in Survivor, so this is a way to use them and hopefully advance to Week 7. With more bye weeks ahead, it’s important to save a few top teams – if possible – for a game that may not be as much of a sure thing. Indy at home against the Titans is by far the most favorable game on the team’s schedule outside of a Nov. 15 home game against Miami. The Titans have been lost to open this season, and I don’t expect them to turn things around any time soon with how abysmal their offense has looked. The Colts may not cover, but they should handle business at home in Week 6. – Peter Dewey New England Patriots The New England Patriots proved last week that they still can show flashes of the team that won the AFC last season, especially when they play the weaker teams in the NFL. Their defense is a top 10 unit and Drake Maye can still torch a below average secondary. The Patriots now rank 10th in EPA per play, while the New York Jets rank 20th. New England is also 11th in opponent success rate, while New York is 23rd. That could all lead to big things for the Patriots in this divisional game. The Patriots have a ton of tough games on their schedule this season, including the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos, so taking them when they're at home against either the Jets or Dolphins is going to be the move, which is why this is the week I'll take them at Gillette Stadium against Geno Smith and Aaron Glenn. Plus, New England is 18-2 at home in its last 20 games against the Jets. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. It will be the first of two meetings between the AFC East rivals, as the Patriots will travel to face the Jets on Dec. 27. It will be a matchup of top-10 defenses with the Patriots entering the contest with the fifth-ranked defense and the Jets ranked fourth in the NFL. The Patriots earned their 24th series sweep of the New York Jets last season and their first against the Jets since the 2022 season. The Patriots beat the Jets, 27-14, in the first meeting of the season in a Thursday Night Football game at Gillette Stadium on Nov. 13, and then behind a 5-touchdown performance by QB Drake Maye, New England beat the Jets 42-10 at MetLife Stadium on Dec. 28, 2025. Related Links How to Watch and Stream Sunday's Patriots Game Against the Jets | NFL Week 6 SERIES HISTORY The New England Patriots and New York Jets will meet for the first of two scheduled meetings when they face off this week at Gillette Stadium. The Patriots will travel to face the Jets on Dec. 27. Last year, the Patriots earned their 24th season sweep with a 27-14 win at home on Nov. 3 and then a 42-10 victory at the Jets on Dec. 28. The Patriots enter this week with three straight wins against the Jets. New England leads the series 77-56-1 overall. The Patriots are 41-26-1 all-time in home games against the Jets, including 21-5 in games played at Gillette Stadium. The teams have played in the postseason three times – a 1985 Wild Card game, a 2006 Wild Card game and an AFC Divisional game in 2010. New England beat the Jets 26-14 in 1985 at the Meadowlands en route to Super Bowl XX. In 2006, the Patriots defeated the Jets 37-16 at Gillette Stadium, and the Jets beat the Patriots 28-21 in the 2010 Divisional playoff game in Foxborough. New England is 48-18 and 25-9 in home games against the Jets since Robert Kraft purchased the team in 1994, including two postseason games. New England's 77 overall victories over the Jets (including two playoff wins) are the second-most over any single opponent, trailing only the 81 all-time wins over Buffalo. In addition to the 2011 season, the Patriots also had back-to-back games with 500 yards in 2008 when they had 511 yards on Nov. 13 vs. the New York Jets and 530 yards on Nov. 23 at Miami. The last time the Patriots had two games with at least 500 yards in the same season was during the 2014 season. The Patriots scored a season-high 45 points in the victory over Las Vegas. If the Patriots have at least 400 yards on offense this week against the Jets, it will be their first three-game stretch with at least 400 yards since closing the 2025 season with three such games: 453 yards at Baltimore (12/21), 440 yards at the N.Y. Jets (12/28) and 457 yards vs. Miami (1/4). The Patriots record for most consecutive games with at least 400 yards is eight during the 2007 season. The Patriots are off to a 2-0 start at Gillette Stadium in 2026. The last time the Patriots started off with a 3-0 home record was during the 2019 season when they won their first five home games. If the Patriots beat the Jets this week, they will start with a 2-0 record in the AFC East. Last season, the Patriots began the year with a 3-0 record against division opponents. If he has 2 touchdowns this week vs. the Jets, he will be the first Patriots player with at least 2 touchdown receptions in back-to-back games since TE Rob Gronkowski accomplished the feat in 2012 when he had 2 touchdown receptions vs. the New York Jets (10/21) and at St. Louis (10/28). The last New England wide receiver with back-to-back games with at least 2 touchdowns was WR Randy Moss in 2007 in the final two games of the season. Weight: 249 lbs College: Arkansas TE Hunter Henry became the fourth Patriots tight end to reach 3,000 receiving yards in the win against Pittsburgh (9/20). Henry enters this week ranked fourth on the team's all-time list for touchdown receptions among tight ends with 27 touchdowns and needs 1 touchdown to tie Russ Francis for third place on the team's all-time list. Jets (10/16), 5 vs. Chicago (10/26) and 4 vs. Denver (11/2). Maye threw for 374 yards last week against the Raiders. If he throws for 300 yards this week against the Jets, he will be the first Patriots quarterback with back-to-back 300- yard games since Tom Brady in 2019 when he threw for 348 yards at Washington (10/6) and 334 yards vs. the New York Giants (10/10). Maye finished 26-of-34 for 374 yards with 4 touchdown passes for a 150.9 passer rating last week against the Raiders. It is the third time he has had a rating of 150 or better. He had a career-best 157.0 rating at the New York Jets on Dec. 28, 2025 and a 155.6 rating vs. Carolina on Sept. 28, 2025. A Patriots player has never had backto-back games with a 150.0 rating or better. The last NFL player to have back-to-back games with a passer rating of 150 or more is Jared Goff with Detroit in 2024 when he had a 155.8 passer rating vs. Seattle (9/30) followed by a 153.8 passer rating at Dallas (10/13). Maye is eighth on the team's all-time list for passing yards with 7,898 yards and needs 102 passing yards against the Jets this week to become the eighth Patriots player to reach 8,000 passing yards. Elijah Ponder Weight: 261 lbs College: Cal Poly LB Elijah Ponder has at least a half sack in four straight games. The last Patriots player with at least a half a sack in five games was LB Josh Uche in 2022. Uche had 1 sack at Minnesota (11/24), 2 sacks vs. Buffalo (12/1), 3 sacks at Arizona (12/12), a half a sack at Las Vegas (12/18) and 1 sack vs. Cincinnati (12/24). It'll be tough for the Jets to replicate their performance in Week 6, as they head on the road to take on the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium, a house of horrors for Gang Green over the past 15 years.
