picks.headline: Patriots-Jets Week 6 preview: Keys to victory, prediction and more
picks.blurb: Patriots-Jets Week 6 preview: Keys to victory, prediction and more – NBC Sports Boston Celtics New England seeks its third straight win. By Justin Leger • Published October 15, 2026 • Updated on October 15, 2026 at 2:49 pm Nov 13, 2025; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (10) looks to pass the ball against the New York Jets in the first quarter at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images The New England Patriots snapped out of their early-season funk with back-to-back impressive wins over the Buffalo Bills and Las Vegas Raiders. Will they stay hot this Sunday against the New York Jets? If Drake Maye plays how he has over the last two weeks, the Jets won't stand much of a chance. The third-year quarterback is back to looking like his MVP-caliber self. He was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week after a 269-yard, three-TD performance vs. Buffalo, and should've earned the honor again after his 374-yard, five-TD gem against Vegas. The Patriots have dominated the Jets for the last two-and-a-half decades, but don't underestimate New York heading into this Week 6 matchup. Its pass defense has been among the NFL's best so far this season, so it won't be easy for Maye to keep his torrid stretch going, even if star wide receiver A.J. Brown is back in the mix. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels may have to lean more on the run game, which would mean a heavy workload for Rhamondre Stevenson with TreVeyon Henderson likely out with an ankle injury . As of Thursday, New England is a 7.5-point favorite to win Sunday's game at Gillette Stadium. What are the keys to matching those expectations? Here's our Pats-Jets Week 6 preview and prediction: Recent head-to-head matchups The Patriots beating up on the Jets is a tradition like no other. They've won 40 of their last 50 regular-season games against their storied AFC East rival since December 2001. They've lost to New York only twice in the last decade. Last season, the Patriots took care of business with a 13-point win at home before blowing the Jets out at MetLife Stadium. Here are the last three Patriots-Jets matchups: Week 11, 2025 at New England: 27-14 Patriots Week 17, 2025 at New York: 42-10 Patriots Week 8, 2024 at New England: 25-22 Patriots View this post on Instagram Key Stats David Bailey is a game-wrecker Jets edge rusher David Bailey could be a problem for the Patriots on Sunday. Bailey has five sacks through the first five weeks of his NFL career, including three in New York's 17-12 win over Cleveland last week. The undrafted rookie also racked up three tackles for loss and four total QB hits to earn the AFC Defensive Player of the Week honor. According to the NFL, Bailey became the first rookie since Jean Phillips with at least three sacks and three TFLs in the same game. David Bailey was a man on a mission in Week 5 🔥 @Pepsi https://t.co/DKOYWjlsLg Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel is well-aware of the challenge Bailey presents. "He's fast, explosive, instinctive," Vrabel said of Bailey on Wednesday. "He can bend, got a really good get off and is able to win at the top and corner. He uses his get off, so just like every week, we'll have to be very conscious of the front." Feed Rhamondre? The Jets have had one of the stingiest pass defenses this season, limiting opponents to an average of 175 passing yards per game (fourth-fewest in NFL). They could make it tough for Maye to push the ball downfield, giving McDaniels no choice but to lean on his running backs. That means we should expect a hefty workload for Rhamondre Stevenson. The Pats' RB2, TreVeyon Henderson, will miss time after suffering a high-ankle sprain last week. Stevenson and Corey Kiner are the only RBs currently on the active roster, though Lan Larison and Hassan Haskins are candidates to be elevated from the practice squad. While the Jets aren't terrible against the run, they're beatable. They rank 13th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (118). Patriots' key to victory Protect Drake Maye The Jets are tied for third in the NFL with 17 sacks this season. As mentioned above, rookie edge rusher David Bailey leads the group with five sacks, three coming last week vs. Cleveland. The Patriots offensive line will be tested against this menacing Jets front, especially if left tackle Will Campbell is out due to the knee injury he suffered last week. "I think they're physical. I think they have tenacity. I think they've got, I wouldn't say a new ferociousness, but you can see the difference on tape from last year," Maye said of the Jets defense on Wednesday. "They have some new faces, some new mentality. I think they're buying into how Coach [Aaron] Glenn wants to play defense, and I think you respect that. "You can see that on film. It pops out to you. They do a good job on the back end, mixing it up and also getting on you and grabbing you and playing physical. So, you can see that they're building something on defense, and it's really shown this year with how they played. Maye struggled mightily over the first three weeks of the season. Uncoincidentally, he was pressured often and sacked nine times in that span. Over his last two stellar games, Maye has only been sacked twice. Jets' key to victory Win the turnover battle The only way we see the Patriots losing to the Jets at home this week is if they fail to protect the football. That's how they earned both of their losses this season, with Maye tossing three interceptions in the season opener vs. Seattle and turning it over four times in Week 3 against Jacksonville. Fortunately for Maye and the Pats, the Jets don't pick anyone off. They went a record 21 games without an interception before safety Minkah Fitzpatrick finally snapped the streak in Week 4. That was New York's only INT so far this year. Fumbles are a different story. The Jets are tied for second in the NFL with five fumble recoveries this season. Maye has fumbled five times, Stevenson lost a fumble in Week 2, and Kiner coughed it up in last week's win. The Patriots must avoid giving the Jets extra possessions. If they do that, they should win this game pretty handily. Over the last two weeks, the Pats have resembled the 2025 team that finished 14-3 and represented the AFC in the Super Bowl. If they're even 75 percent as good as they were against Buffalo and Las Vegas, they should breeze past New York at home. That said, the Jets defense is capable of keeping this one close, especially if key Pats players are sidelined due to injuries. Running back TreVeyon Henderson and left tackle Will Campbell are expected to be out, and it remains to be seen whether star wideout A.J. Brown is ready to return from injured reserve. This could be a tougher matchup than many anticipate. But even if the Patriots are forced to embrace the "next man up" mentality yet again, a decent performance from Maye should be enough to propel them to 4-2. away.blurb: The loss doesn't seem to be just in the standings for the Browns now, as reports come out of it that they saw both running back Quinshon Judkins and linebacker Carson Schqesinger leave in walking boots. Cleveland.com's Mary Kay Cabot was the one to share this information after the game. On Monday, we didn't have an update on Judkins, but NFL Media's Ian Rapoport shared one on Schwesinger. He posted on social media, saying, "Browns star LB Carson Schwesinger suffered a Grade 1 ankle sprain in their loss against the Jets, though the injury occurred before his strip sack of Geno Smith, sources say. He is not ruled out for this week, though availability depends on how he responds." The idea of the Browns' defense losing Schwesinger for any amount of time would be devastating. The team has the Baltimore Ravens next up on the schedule, who are dealing with injuries of their own, but they need him for them and more.

away.headline: New York Jets' Blitz Rate Is a Risk Against Patriots QB Drake Maye
away.blurb: The potential return of Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) raises the stakes. Locked On Patriots host Nick Cattles said Brown had returned to practice after the team opened his 21-day window, though his availability and workload remained unclear. Butchko said Brown’s presence would force the Jets to alter their coverage approach even if he plays a limited role because New York lacks the true shutdown corner it once had with Sauce Gardner. – Tight end Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) returned to practice in a limited capacity, according to Butchko. He argued the Jets need to simplify the rookie’s role and create more intermediate-field opportunities if he is cleared, particularly with Breece Hall and Adonai Mitchell expected to miss the game. The New York Jets may need to abandon the volume of defensive pressure that helped them beat Cleveland when they visit the New England Patriots on Sunday. Locked On Jets host John Butchko pointed to New York’s blitz rate in Week 5 and argued that repeatedly sending extra rushers at Patriots quarterback Drake Maye would leave the Jets liable to big plays. (Butchko referred to the blitz rate as 47%, but TruMedia listed it as 52.3%.) Butchko said Maye’s mobility and success against pressure make this a different assignment from the rain-soaked matchup against the Browns. The Jets can still create a turnover by disguising pressure and picking their spots, but an overemphasis on the blitz would give Maye chances to extend plays and attack openings in the secondary. A more selective rush would put greater responsibility on the secondary to cover longer, especially if Brown is active. The Jets have received better-than-expected early contributions from cornerbacks Azareye’h Thomas and Brandon Stephens, plus safety Dane Belton, but Maye presents a more demanding test when he can escape the initial pressure. The counterargument is clear: Sitting back too often could give Maye a clean pocket and allow the Patriots to sustain their explosive-play offense. New York’s answer may be to vary its looks rather than make pressure the defining feature of every passing down. For a defense that has protected its red zone well, preventing a few vertical completions could matter more than chasing sacks. The Jets have a path to a second straight win if they make Maye work through tight windows, limit the Patriots’ explosive plays and avoid letting one coverage bust turn an aggressive call into a momentum swing. – Wide receiver Garrett Wilson will draw a major individual test from Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), who returned to practice after missing the past two games. home.headline: New York Jets' Blitz Rate Is a Risk Against Patriots QB Drake Maye
home.blurb: The potential return of Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) raises the stakes. Locked On Patriots host Nick Cattles said Brown had returned to practice after the team opened his 21-day window, though his availability and workload remained unclear. Butchko said Brown’s presence would force the Jets to alter their coverage approach even if he plays a limited role because New York lacks the true shutdown corner it once had with Sauce Gardner. – Tight end Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) returned to practice in a limited capacity, according to Butchko. He argued the Jets need to simplify the rookie’s role and create more intermediate-field opportunities if he is cleared, particularly with Breece Hall and Adonai Mitchell expected to miss the game. The New York Jets may need to abandon the volume of defensive pressure that helped them beat Cleveland when they visit the New England Patriots on Sunday. Locked On Jets host John Butchko pointed to New York’s blitz rate in Week 5 and argued that repeatedly sending extra rushers at Patriots quarterback Drake Maye would leave the Jets liable to big plays. (Butchko referred to the blitz rate as 47%, but TruMedia listed it as 52.3%.) Butchko said Maye’s mobility and success against pressure make this a different assignment from the rain-soaked matchup against the Browns. The Jets can still create a turnover by disguising pressure and picking their spots, but an overemphasis on the blitz would give Maye chances to extend plays and attack openings in the secondary. A more selective rush would put greater responsibility on the secondary to cover longer, especially if Brown is active. The Jets have received better-than-expected early contributions from cornerbacks Azareye’h Thomas and Brandon Stephens, plus safety Dane Belton, but Maye presents a more demanding test when he can escape the initial pressure. The counterargument is clear: Sitting back too often could give Maye a clean pocket and allow the Patriots to sustain their explosive-play offense. New York’s answer may be to vary its looks rather than make pressure the defining feature of every passing down. For a defense that has protected its red zone well, preventing a few vertical completions could matter more than chasing sacks. The Jets have a path to a second straight win if they make Maye work through tight windows, limit the Patriots’ explosive plays and avoid letting one coverage bust turn an aggressive call into a momentum swing. – Wide receiver Garrett Wilson will draw a major individual test from Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), who returned to practice after missing the past two games. Butchko said New York’s depleted receiver group leaves little margin if Gonzalez can limit Wilson’s targets. Some or all of this content may have been generated by AI. However, having Gonzalez available would provide greater flexibility in coverage and potentially reduce the need to compensate for missing personnel elsewhere. Hall missed Thursday's practice, leaving questions about whether New York will have one of its most dangerous offensive players available. picks.headline: NFL predictions: Will underdog Giants upend the Saints?
picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Will underdog Giants upend the Saints? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team NFL predictions: Will underdog Giants upend the Saints? Ed Valentine Thu, October 15, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Can the New York Giants, 3-0 at MetLife Stadium this season, continue their winning ways at home on Sunday when they face the New Orleans Saints? Below, how the Big Blue View staff is predicting the game, as well as the rest of the NFL Week 6 action. Just how beaten up are the Giants? That's the question on my mind as we get ready for this game. I think I'm less concerned with Abdul Carter than I am with Andrew Thomas and Jermaine Eluemunor. Even though Thomas hasn't been healthy since Week 1, the Giants have still fielded one of the very best tackle duos in the NFL. And while Marcus Mbow has played well in his outing, he's struggled with power in the past. That's a bit of a concern given the Saints have a pair of good-sized and powerful defensive ends in Chase Young and Carl Granderson. That said, the Saints' defense has been pretty porous and their win rates haven't been great this year. As long as the Giants can protect Jameis Winston, there should be opportunities to move the ball and score. On the flip side, the Giants' defense has been playing with a similar aggression as the Vikings' defense that held Tyler Shough to 3.8 yards per attempt, and their offense to 142 total yards. The Giants' pass rush has been dynamic over the last two games, and they've been opportunistic in creating turnovers. The Giants' athletic blitzers could cause many of the same problems for the Saints as the Vikings' did — at least assuming Abdul Carter's calf injury is minor. I'm still going to pick the Giants to win the game, but my confidence level depends on the the Giants' health. Tony Del Genio This is an uncomfortable matchup for the Giants. The Saints have been sub-.500 in three of the past four seasons, yet they have beaten the Giants three years in a row. The Giants' last victory was in overtime in 2021, when Daniel Jones passed for 402 yards in the Superdome. The losing quarterback in that game was…Jameis Winston. History aside, my discomfort stems from what I see as a non-ideal matchup of strengths and weaknesses. Tyler Shough is a very experienced quarterback even though this is only his second year in the NFL. His receiving corps is better than what the Giants saw last week, most notably Chris Olave, second in the NFL in receiving yards. Shough was flummoxed by Brian Flores' blitzing Minnesota defense last week. If that sounds like good news because Dennard Wilson has become fond of the blitz himself, it's not. Flores' defense works because the zone defense and deception he uses behind it induce quarterbacks to throw quickly to receivers they think are open, but aren't. Dennard instead is playing a decent amount of Cover 0 and leaving cornerbacks to stay with receivers in single coverage. Can the Giants' cornerbacks cover receivers like Olave? The answer to that may decide the game. I'm more optimistic about the Giants on offense…if they can protect Winston. Chase Young is back to his early form, and with Carl Granderson on the other side form a good 1-2 punch against…whom? Neither Andrew Thomas nor Jermaine Eluemunor practiced on Wednesday. If Winston sees a lot of pressure, it could be lights out for the Giants. Given time, though, he may be able to exploit the Saints' second and third levels. And maybe the Giants can find a way to finally run the ball effectively against one of the worst run defenses in the league. I choose to be optimistic this week. A little, anyway. David Hartman I'm more than a little surprised that the 1-4 Saints are favored over the 3-1-1 Giants this Sunday, and especially with the game being played at MetLife. Then again, while the Giants are 2-0-1 in their last three outings, all of those games were effectively decided on the final play of the game. New York is a bounce (and brain fart) or two away from also being 1-4. The Saints are Big Blue's fourth straight opponent who, like them, picked in the Top-10 of the 2026 draft, with three of those four games at home. This game is the end of the easy stretch of New York's schedule. New Orleans can throw the ball, but they can't run it or stop the run. They rank 30th in the NFL in rushing offense and 29th in rushing defense. Kellen Moore's offense is fast-paced — they're second in the league in plays per game (74). Dennard Wilson's defense will need to stay fresh, and play better than it did last week against Washington. Sustained drives by New York's offense should help with that. I like the Giants to win fairly convincingly in this one, and for the first time in a month, I don't think you'll need to wear a heart monitor to watch the fourth quarter. They should be able to establish the run and work some play-action off of that, and I think they'll be able to rattle Tyler Shough with their pass rush, as the Vikings did last week. Jameis Winston didn't throw any picks last week (although he did lose a fumble) and while it's a lot to ask for a repeat, I think he's showing pretty good command and very good rapport with his main weapons. They'll get a lift from the home crowd too. The Giants come home Sunday to face a the New Orleans Saints, a team that has been put on notice by their owner just this week that improvements are needed. I do not know about you, but when my boss tells me something like that, my work goes up a notch. As Jon Runyan noted this week, the Giants could easily be 1-4 and they are a beat up team coming off their tie in Washington— there is a real chance that their offensive tackles could be a first- and second-year player at some point on Sunday. When teams are evenly matched, I always go with the more desperate team and the Giants using up all of their luck last week. Pick: Saints 27, Giants 10 Valentine's View Like others above, this game makes be a bit queasy from a Giants' perspective. They have lost to the Saints three years in a row. The 1-4 Saints are likely better than their record, and are under fire from ownership . They will come to MetLife Stadium desperate to turn their season around. The Giants are 3-0 at home this season, but you are fooling yourself if you think they will win every game at MetLife. The Saints are vulnerable defensively and middling offensively, but the Giants have plenty of their own issues. I think the Giants can find a way to win this game. Perhaps that comes down to the belief in themselves the Giants have developed vs. a Saints team that has underperformed expectations. I feel like, at least for now, things have been bouncing the Giants way. If Abdul Carter can't play, though, my view on this game might change. Giants fans: Make your pick in the SB Nation app! picks.headline: Experts Unanimously Pick Giants to Defeat Saints in Week 6
picks.blurb: Experts Unanimously Pick Giants to Defeat Saints in Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Experts Unanimously Pick Giants to Defeat Saints in Week 6 (Amber Searls-Imagn Images) Matt Levine Thu, October 15, 2026 at 7:26 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants will enter Week 6 of the NFL season holding a record of 3-1-1 following a strange ending last week. The Giants tied with the Washington Commanders in what ended up being one of the weirder games of the season. New York should have lost to Washington, so the fact that they tied is being taken as a win for the team. But the Giants know that they will need a better effort going forward this week as the team gets ready to face off against the New Orleans Saints at home. New Orleans will be coming into the game looking to stop the bleeding, with the Saints sitting with a record of 1-4 on the year. Both sides need a win this week for different reasons, and the Giants will try to remain perfect at home this season. New York can't overlook this Saints team despite their struggles this season; otherwise, the Giants could find themselves in a tight contest. Bleacher Report did game predictions for every contest this week, with Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford picking. In these predictions, every single expert went with the Giants to take down New Orleans. Much of this could be due to the Saints having their own problems this year, but the Giants have shown real promise as a team. Even with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart going down with an injury, the Giants have been able to stay the course. Backup signal-caller Jameis Winston has held down the fort well for New York, showing that he can get this team to the playoffs. But the problem with Winston is that he has been very inconsistent over the years in his career, and the Giants know this from the first few weeks of the season. As he gets ready to face off against New Orleans, Winston will need to make sure to stay focused. Winston can be very turnover-prone at times, and the Giants can't afford any issues against the Saints this week. The Giants defense has been a calling card for the team this season, helping them win a few games. And going against an explosive Saints passing attack, the New York secondary will need to be ready to go. The kickoff for the game between the Giants and Saints is scheduled for 10:00 a.m. PT/1:00 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey

picks.headline: Saints vs. Giants Preview: New Orleans Looks to End Losing Streak Against New York
picks.blurb: Saints vs. Giants Preview: New Orleans Looks to End Losing Streak Against New York - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Photo by: Stephen Lew Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:01 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New Orleans Saints travel to MetLife Stadium on Sunday to face the New York Giants in a Week 6 matchup featuring two teams heading in different directions. New Orleans is looking to snap a three-game losing streak, while New York hopes to continue its strong start under first-year head coach John Harbaugh. The Saints enter the matchup at 1-4 after falling 23-13 to the Minnesota Vikings last week. The Giants are 3-1-1 after an exciting 27-27 overtime tie against the Washington Commanders. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Tyler Shough Leads the Saints New Orleans will rely on quarterback Tyler Shough to help get its offense back on track. The second-year quarterback has shown the ability to make plays through the air, but the Saints have struggled to find consistency during their recent losing streak. Through five games, Shough has thrown for 1,299 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions. He will need to make smart decisions and avoid turnovers against a Giants defense that has shown it can pressure opposing quarterbacks. Wide receiver Chris Olave remains one of New Orleans' most important offensive weapons. His ability to create separation and make plays downfield could be crucial as the Saints try to stretch the Giants' defense. Running back Alvin Kamara is another key player to watch. Establishing a productive rushing attack would help New Orleans create a more balanced offense and prevent New York from focusing primarily on Shough and the passing game. Head coach Kellen Moore needs his team to execute more consistently after the Saints managed just 142 total yards against Minnesota. Jameis Winston and the Giants Look to Build Momentum The Giants enter Sunday's game with confidence after rallying from a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit against Washington before settling for a tie. Quarterback Jameis Winston has stepped into the starting role and helped spark the offense. Against Washington, Winston led the Giants to 24 points on their four full drives in the third and fourth quarters, giving New York a chance to complete the comeback. The Giants also have playmakers capable of creating problems for New Orleans. Wide receiver Malik Nabers gives Winston a dangerous target, while tight end Isaiah Likely provides another option in the passing game. Harbaugh has emphasized his team's resilience, and the Giants will look to carry that mentality into their return home. A Key Matchup in the Trenches One of the biggest factors could be New York's pass rush against New Orleans' offensive line. If the Giants consistently pressure Shough, the Saints could struggle to sustain drives. New Orleans, meanwhile, needs its defense to contain Winston and prevent the Giants from producing the explosive plays that helped fuel their comeback last week. What to Watch Sunday The Saints need a complete performance to end their losing streak, while the Giants have an opportunity to strengthen their position in the NFC East. With Shough trying to steady New Orleans' offense and Winston leading a resilient Giants team, quarterback play and execution on third down could be decisive in this Week 6 matchup.

away.headline: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve
away.blurb: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve Welcome back, Zach Wood. The New Orleans Saints long snapper was a full participant at practice on Wednesday, marking his return from injured reserve. He'll need to continue practicing throughout the week in order to be activated for Sunday's game with the New York Giants , but all signs point to him snapping the ball at MetLife Stadium. The Saints released fill-in long snapper Cal Adomitis and don't have another player at the position on their roster. They also left a vacancy open and waiting for Wood on the 53-man roster once he gets the green light. Wood, 33, won the job back in 2017 and was the long snapper for New Orleans in 150 consecutive regular season games (plus seven playoff games), finally ending his streak when a calf strain forced him out of action the last four weeks. The fear was that he would have needed even more time to recover, but he's ahead of schedule and expected to be back in the lineup. Wood has made quite a career for himself as a former rookie free agent out of SMU. He actually spent some time with the Dallas Cowboys when Kellen Moore was the backup quarterback in 2016 and part of the 2017 preseason. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve John Sigler, Saints Wire Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:56 AM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads He's been missed. Adomitis had some hiccups and drew an untimely penalty during Week 5's loss to the Minnesota Vikings , so getting Wood back on the field should help steady the operation. You just hope he isn't rushing himself back too soon.

away.headline: Vikings-Saints Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, some intrigue with a number of players listed as questionable, including Jordan Addison, Justin Jefferson, and Brian O’Neill. I’m gonna go out on a limb and say that all three will play on Sunday. I know they will be cautious with all of them, but it doesn’t sound like Jefferson has experienced any problems with his ankle all week. It sounds like Addison and O’Neill’s injuries are more of the minor variety they will play through. It’s not a surprise at this point that Christian Darrisaw is out, as he hadn’t practiced all week. He should be ready to go after the bye week. For the Saints, Alvin Kamara is questionable but my guess is he’ll play on Sunday. Safety Julian Blackmon is also questionable but probably will play as well. Those are the two key players on the Saints list this week. Everyone else is either listed as out or do not have a deisignation and/or are a backup. Who will be sitting this one out? home.headline: NY Giants injury report: Abdul Carter held out of practice for 2nd straight day
home.blurb: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin), right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and edge defender Abdul Carter (calf) all worked on the side with trainers Thursday during the media viewing portion of New York Giants practice. All three, along with cornerback Colton Hood (concussion) and safety Tyler Nubin (neck) were officially listed as “did not practice.” Linebacker Malik Harrison, who was just added to the 53-man roster this week, was added to the injury report with a groin issue. He was a limited participant. For Thomas, who has been managing his injury since Week 2 against the Los Angeles Rams, this has been his weekly routine. He has yet to miss a snap due to the injury. If Carter is not able to play Sunday against the New Orleans Saints, that would be a massive blow to a Giants’ defense already without star edge defender Brian Burns (torn ACL) for the season. Carter has 2.0 sacks, and is tied sixth in the NFL among edge defenders and linebackers with 14 quarterback pressures. Carter leads the league with 11 ‘quick’ quarterback pressures, defined as pressures achieved in less than 2.5 seconds. If Eluemunor cannot play, Marcus Mbow would start at right tackle and rookie J.C. Davis would be the swing tackle. Safety Jason Pinnock, who missed last week’s game due to a concussion, was a full practice participant. That is good news, especially with Nubin trending toward not playing.

home.blurb: The Saints did receive some encouraging news, as edge rusher Tyree Wilson and defensive tackle Colby Wooden returned to full participation after being limited Wednesday. Alvin Kamara 's status also warrants attention after the veteran running back was limited for the second consecutive practice with a back injury. New Orleans' front seven faces depth concerns as Elliss (calf) and Anfernee Jennings (knee) missed practice for a second straight day, joining sidelined defensive tackle Shepherd (illness) and limited lineman Vernon Broughton (illness). However, Wooden (toe) and Wilson (ankle) returned to full participation Thursday. Those developments provide some encouragement for a defense needing its front seven operating near full strength. However, the Giants received encouraging news regarding wide receiver Darnell Mooney and safety Jason Pinnock , both of whom improved from limited to full participation Thursday. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. The 76 straight games played without a losing record was the longest streak in team history. The overall NFL record is 145 by the Patriots from 2003-12. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024. They're coming off a brilliant upset win over the Detroit Lions, too. The Philadelphia Eagles made the long trek back from London after a mindboggling, crushing defeat where victory was essentially secured. The Panthers have the advantage this week, it seems. Despite that, they're not favored on the road, and some experts aren't willing to pick the Panthers to take the Eagles down. Expert picks for Eagles vs. Panthers in NFL Week 6 action Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni reacts during the first half | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. "The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense," he wrote. His CBS colleague, Jordan Dajani, disagreed, picking the Panthers to win 23-21. "The Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS," Dajani pointed out. Here's how SI's staff is picking the game: Albert Breer:Panthers Eva Geitheim: Panthers Mitch Goldich: Eagles Mike Kadlick: Panthers Gilberto Manzano: Panthers Conor Orr: Eagles John Pluym: Eagles Matt Verderame: Eagles Bleacher Report's Wes O'Donnell is taking the Panthers to cover the spread and win outright. "I'm done trying to figure out the Eagles. The Eagles clearly cannot figure out the Eagles. And while the Panthers' defense is a great opportunity for any offense to get right, Carolina had a bye week and then some to prepare for Philly. This Panthers team has defied the odds and shown up in tough situations since last season," he wrote. Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales reacts after the game at Bank of America Stadium | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles. At ESPN , only Pam Maldonado and Dan Graziano picked the Eagles to beat the Panthers. The Athletic's Vic Tafur was obscenely blunt: "The Eagles are coming off two heartbreaking losses, they struggle against play-action passes (a Panthers staple), and it wouldn't shock me if this is Sirianni's last game as head coach." What does this mean? Despite the overwhelming advantages the Panthers have in this game, there's still a perception that the Eagles are the Eagles and the Panthers are the woeful Panthers. That makes Week 6's contest a perfect opportunity to reshape the narrative, although it's a little unfair that a primetime victory over the Detroit Lions didn't do that for the Panthers. picks.headline: Panthers vs. Eagles Preview: Carolina Looks to Take Advantage of Philadelphia’s Struggles
picks.blurb: Panthers vs. Eagles Preview: Carolina Looks to Take Advantage of Philadelphia’s Struggles - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Photo by: Bob Donnan Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 7:57 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Carolina Panthers travel to Philadelphia on Sunday for an important Week 6 matchup against the Eagles, with both teams looking to get their seasons moving in the right direction. Carolina enters the game at 2-2 following a bye week, while Philadelphia sits at 2-3 after suffering three consecutive losses. The Eagles are coming off a heartbreaking 17-16 defeat against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, where a late field goal sealed another frustrating result. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET at Lincoln Financial Field, with the game airing on CBS. Bryce Young Leads Carolina's Offense Panthers quarterback Bryce Young will be one of the biggest players to watch Sunday. Young has shown significant improvement during the 2026 season, helping Carolina develop a more productive passing attack. His connection with rookie wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan has become an important part of the offense, giving the Panthers a dangerous combination through the air. Carolina's offense looked particularly effective in its victory over the Detroit Lions before the bye week. Young will look to carry that momentum into Philadelphia against an Eagles defense that has struggled to consistently close out games. Head coach Dave Canales will also want to establish the running game and keep Young in manageable situations. If Carolina can maintain balance offensively, it could create opportunities to attack Philadelphia downfield. Tanner McKee Takes Over for Philadelphia Philadelphia faces a significant challenge at quarterback after Jalen Hurts was ruled out because of a superficial blood clot in his leg. Backup Tanner McKee is expected to start in his place. McKee has limited NFL starting experience, making Sunday's matchup an important opportunity for him to demonstrate what he can do against Carolina's defense. Head coach Nick Sirianni will need to put McKee in favorable situations while finding ways to generate offense despite the team's recent struggles. Philadelphia's offensive line has also undergone significant changes, and the Eagles have struggled to establish their usual rushing attack. Getting the running game going could help take pressure off McKee and allow the offense to find a rhythm. An Important NFC Matchup For Carolina, Sunday's game represents an opportunity to take advantage of an Eagles team dealing with several challenges and return from the bye with a statement victory. Philadelphia desperately needs to stop its losing streak and regain confidence at home. With Young leading Carolina's offense and McKee stepping into a starting role for the Eagles, execution and turnovers could play major roles in determining the outcome. Both teams have plenty to prove, making Sunday's matchup an important test for their respective seasons.

home.blurb: According to NFL insider Mike Garafolo , Smith was upgraded to limited participant on Thursday and there is still optimism he will play in Week 6. The Eagles have been relying on wide receivers Darius Cooper, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon with Smith out, and it is safe to say they would welcome him back with open arms after he began the season with 19 catches for 235 yards and one touchdown. Philadelphia Eagles star wide receiver DeVonta Smith was originally reported as a non-participant during the team’s latest practice with the hamstring injury that has kept him sidelined for the past two games. However, the Eagles revealed that wasn’t necessarily the case with their latest injury report. If the Eagles could get Smith back for this week’s matchup against the Carolina Panthers, it would certainly be some much-needed reinforcements. Philadelphia will already be without quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clot), and running back Saquon Barkley will likely join him in due time as he continues to battle his way through a hamstring injury as well. However, that also begs the question of whether it would be worth it to risk Smith re-injurying himself if the offense is going to be without a couple of its top players. The Eagles still have a few days to make that decision, though. Sunday’s Week 6 matchup against the Panthers will kick off at 1 p.m. ET. Yes. Yes. Let me say it again: Yes. After a horror show in Week 4 with my NFL picks , I got back on track in a big way this past week. I was 10-4-1 straight up and 9-6-1 against the spread. That brings my season record straight up to 48-30-1 and the ATS record to 34-43-2. The ATS mark will be a slow climb to get back above .500 after that really bad Week 3. But I felt good about the picks this week. Time to build some momentum. Two good weeks in a row? All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) London on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Jaguars will have been in London for two weeks, which makes this a challenge for the Texans , who went this week. Houston won for the first time on the road last week and now their division chances probably rest on this game. The Jaguars were sloppy last week, which will get them back focused. Jaguars will win a tight one. Pick: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons (+3) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a horrible showing in Green Bay, in which the defense was shredded. But the Falcons lost in overtime to the Ravens and quarterback Michael Penix was hurt. He will likely play here, and that's a good thing since he can light up the Chicago defense. Falcons win it. Pick: Falcons 27, Bears 21 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns There is a chance that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will be back for this game after missing last week with an ankle injury. Even if he isn't, I think the Ravens defense will be up to the task of slowing down the Browns offense. If Jackson is back, the Ravens offense will move the ball. Pick: Ravens 24, Browns 13 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts (-7) The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game. Pick: Colts 28, Titans 17 New York Jets at New England Patriots (-7.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Patriots have turned their season around with consecutive victories as Drake Maye has come alive. The Jets played better on defense against Cleveland last week with eight sacks, but this is a bigger challenge. Look for Maye to keep it going as the Pats win a third straight. Pick: Patriots 28, Jets 13 New Orleans Saints at New York Giants (+1.5) The Saints have lost three straight and have fallen to 1-4. They didn't play well against the Vikings last week, but this is a chance to get right. The Giants tied last week, but Jameis Winston played well. I think this will be about defenses. Giants in a close one. Pick: Giants 19, Saints 16 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense. Pick: Eagles 23, Panthers 20 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3) Both of these teams righted the ship a bit with victories last week. The Bucs badly needed it after losing their first four. Tampa Bay ran it with Bucky Irving to beat the Cowboys and I think they can do that here as well. The defense played better in that game and will limit Aaron Rodgers somewhat. Bucs win it. Pick: Bucs 26, Steelers 21 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams (-13.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The "Dream Team" Rams are 2-3 and haven't looked the part of a Super Bowl champ. The offense got it going against the Bills , but the defense was a non-factor in the fourth quarter and overtime. They will play better here against the Cardinals . Meanwhile, Matt Stafford will have a big day. Pick: Rams 35, Cardinals 20 Los Angeles Chargers (+8.5) at Kansas City Chiefs Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chargers limp into this one at 0-5, while the Chiefs are undefeated off a bye. The Chargers are desperate and need a win or their season will be over. This is not a good place to try to get that first victory. Look for Patrick Mahomes to play well. Chiefs coach Andy Reid is outstanding in his career off a bye. Pick: Chiefs 28, Chargers 21 Buffalo Bills (-6) at Las Vegas Raiders The Bills are playing consecutive road games, but they stayed on the West Coast after beating the Rams in overtime Monday night. That was a tough, physical game, which will make it a challenge on a short week. The Raiders were awful against the Pats, but they will play better on offense here. They just won't stop the Bills. Pick: Bills 35, Raiders 21 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Packers blew out the Bears Sunday as Jordan Love lit up the skies. Look for more of that in this one against a bad Dallas secondary. The Cowboys struggled on defense against the Bucs, and that will continue in this one. Love continues to play well. Packers win a shootout. Pick: Packers 31, Cowboys 27 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a long road trip for the Commanders off a brutal tie last week to face the league's best team right now. That's a tough combination. They can only hope for a letdown by the 49ers after they beat Seattle last week. It won't happen. The 49ers continue to roll as Brock Purdy continues to make a claim as a legitimate MVP candidate. Pick: 49ers 30, Commanders 21 Seattle Seahawks (-3) at Denver Broncos Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Seahawks lost a tough one to the 49ers last week and now face a short week on the road against Denver. The Broncos ' offense has struggled, even with Sean Payton taking over as the play-caller. Bo Nix has to pick it up, but this is a tough defense to try and fix things. Seattle takes a tough road game. picks.blurb: Analyst Predicts Steelers to Dominate Buccaneers in Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Analyst Predicts Steelers to Dominate Buccaneers in Week 6 Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers in a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11, 2026 -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Aaron Becker Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:38 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A NFL analyst is all in on the Pittsburgh Steelers for Week 6. The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently 2.5-point favorites for their Week 6 road game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. However, NFL analyst Conor Orr thinks the oddsmakers have it completely wrong. Orr predicts the Steelers will continue their hot streak and dominate the Buccaneers in Week 6. "I wanna see the Steelers go down to Tampa Bay and win another one of these games," Orr said . "I think they can win this game by three touchdowns." Orr has done a complete 180 in just a matter of a week. Heading into Week 5, he begged the Indianapolis Colts to put the Steelers out of their misery. "Clearly you have communication issues. Your coach came out and said your house is dirty and you need to clean your house. Something's a mess here," Orr said on the Heed the Call NFL Podcast . "I'm sick of [Aaron Rodgers]. I'm sick of watching this team. I'm sick of the receivers dropping balls. I'm sick of them having played one good game against the Bengals so we've got to take them seriously for another three weeks. Come on, Jonathan Taylor. Put up 400 yards and put his old, dying horse out of its misery and off my screen." However, after watching the Steelers offense come alive in their latest win, Orr issued an apology to the team and now seems to be a big believer in Pittsburgh. "I have totally done a 180, and I'll admit it, on this Steelers offense," Orr continued. "Down so many people, and even down to Ben Skowronek, this team has been able to find a way to manufacture points. Aaron Rodgers will have bad Rodgers games, but I've totally flipped on this." The Steelers do seem to have some new found life. Rodgers is playing very well and running back Jaylen Warren has been on another level, recording 176, 126 and 188-yard performances the past three weeks. The only question that remains is: Can the Steelers offense continue this type of production the rest of the season? picks.headline: Steelers vs. Buccaneers Preview: Pittsburgh Travels to Tampa for Crucial Week 6 Matchup
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Buccaneers Preview: Pittsburgh Travels to Tampa for Crucial Week 6 Matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Photo by: Charles LeClaire Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 8:10 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers travel to Florida on Sunday to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in an important Week 6 matchup between two teams looking to build momentum. Pittsburgh enters the game at 3-2, while Tampa Bay is 1-4 after finally earning its first victory of the season. The Buccaneers are coming off an impressive 24-16 road win over the Dallas Cowboys, while the Steelers are looking to get back on track in a competitive AFC North race. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET at Raymond James Stadium, with the game airing on CBS. Aaron Rodgers Leads Pittsburgh's Offense Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers remains one of the biggest storylines heading into Sunday's matchup. The veteran quarterback is playing his 18th NFL season and brings plenty of experience to a Pittsburgh offense that has shown flashes of success. Rodgers' ability to read defenses, make adjustments at the line of scrimmage and deliver accurate passes will be important against a Tampa Bay defense looking to build on its performance against Dallas. Head coach Mike Tomlin will want his offense to establish consistency early. Pittsburgh has alternated wins and losses through its first five games, making Sunday's contest an opportunity to gain momentum before the season progresses further. The Steelers will also look to take advantage of their defensive talent, particularly their ability to pressure opposing quarterbacks and disrupt offensive rhythm. Jalon Daniels Looks to Continue Tampa Bay's Turnaround Tampa Bay will likely turn to rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels , who has stepped into a starting role while Baker Mayfield deals with a thumb injury. Daniels helped lead the Buccaneers to their first win of the season against Dallas, and the team will hope he can build on that performance against Pittsburgh. Head coach Todd Bowles has emphasized physical football, and Tampa Bay's running game was a major factor in its victory over the Cowboys. The Buccaneers rushed for more than 240 yards and forced three turnovers, providing a formula they will look to repeat Sunday. However, facing Pittsburgh's defense presents a different challenge. Daniels will need to protect the football and avoid putting the Buccaneers in difficult situations. Key Matchups to Watch The battle in the trenches could determine how this game unfolds. Pittsburgh will look to pressure Daniels, while Tampa Bay must find ways to protect its young quarterback and maintain its productive rushing attack. The Steelers also need to contain Tampa Bay's playmakers and avoid allowing explosive runs to change the game's momentum. An Important Test for Both Teams Sunday's matchup gives Pittsburgh an opportunity to improve its road performance and strengthen its position in the AFC North. Tampa Bay, meanwhile, will try to turn its victory over Dallas into its first winning streak of the season. With Rodgers' experience facing Daniels' opportunity to establish himself, the quarterback matchup adds another layer of intrigue to Sunday's contest.

picks.blurb: Buccaneers, Steelers: Week 6 game preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Buccaneers, Steelers: Week 6 game preview Aug 16, 2025; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving (7) catches a touchdown pass in front of Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson (41) during the first quarter at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Will Walsh Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Week 6 is set to be rolling into living rooms all throughout the nation and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are no longer winless. Todd Bowles and his pewter pirates managed to pull out a sensationally shocking upset of the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football. Behind the mighty galloping of Bucky Irving and the poise of UDFA Jalen Daniels, Tampa's marauders took over AT&T Stadium. This Sunday (for the third week in a row), it'll be another classic blueblood NFL franchise on the schedule for the Buccaneers— The Pittsburgh Steelers. "The offense can't score if they don't have the ball." How can the Buccaneers win? ARLINGTON, TX - OCTOBER 08: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on October 8, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bucs need to make sure they stay on schedule and stick to their gameplan. There are NFL teams that have the benefit of being able to get into different types of games and win in a variety of ways— The Buccaneers are not that team. If a win is in the cards, they need to make sure they are playing the hand that best suits them. Last week, in Dallas, Tampa did a phenomenal job of staying in the realm of football that they themselves are comfortable playing. The Buccaneers kept the ball on the ground, dominated time of possession— Starting with a 10-minute opening drive, and kept Dallas off-kilter. That dictation was not only an advantage for Tampa Bay, it's the reason they won. That in turn made the Cowboys play the game the Buccaneers needed to play, not the one Dallas wanted to play. It would be easy to say, 'If Bucky Irving rushes for nearly 200 yards, the Buccaneers have a good chance of winning' , but it's more than the yards on the stat sheet. Irving's performance was eye-popping, but it was the offense's ability to stay on the field that won Tampa Bay the game. The Buccaneers finished the game with just shy of 40 minutes time of possession, while Dallas' heralded offense held the ball for just 20. That discrepancy is catastrophic for any team to be on the wrong side of— Personified through the consistent cutaways by Amazon's broadcast as they kept showing defeated, disengaged, and dispirited Dallas Cowboys on the sideline. Consecutive weeks with 40 minutes of possession may not be on the docket, however, will the Buccaneers' offense be able to keep themselves steady, avoid turnovers, and push Pittsburgh to play the type of game Tampa wants to play? "The question isn't who is going to let me; it's who is going to stop me." How can the Buccaneers lose? The Steelers have had some inconsistent offense this year, but they've had 24-plus points in each of the last three weeks (30, 24, 34). Of course, they can't score if they don't play (See the above portion of this article). The Buccaneers' second best option for keeping Pittsburgh's points down, besides pilfering clock, is turnovers. Tampa's turnover differential on the season is not glamourous (-2). Maybe even more absurd, that hideous -2 sits boldly after the Bucs just had a +3 in their last contest. Aside from points themselves, nothing has ever been, or will ever be, a more clear determinant of wins and losses than turnovers. Teams that take the ball away win a lot more than teams that lose the ball. Having the ball means having more chances to score, more chances to score means more better odds you will score; ergo, turnovers are good. More importantly, for a struggling, very one-dimensional team like the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, turnovers level the playing field. The scenario is two-fold. Not only does it fall on your defense to force them, but your offense must avoid turnovers like a coach on the hot seat must avoid losing. Last week, Tampa hit the trifecta— Their defense (and special teams) took the ball away from Dallas three times. Jalen Daniels and the Bucs' offense did not turn the ball over at all and their coach on the heat seat avoided a loss. This week, it's not Dak Prescott it's Aaron Rodgers. Aaron Rodgers is a historically anti-turnover prone quarterback. The former Packers' legend, Jets' bust, and current Steelers' stopgap, has quite literally the greatest touchdown to interception ratio in NFL history— As in, number one. Rodgers is not the type of quarterback that you want to face if the gameplan is get the ball— however , against all odds, Tampa Bay's ever assailed head coach Todd Bowles has actually had a healthy level of success against Rodgers during his Bucs' tenure. The two haven't matched up since Rodgers left Green Bay, but the duels have actually largely favored Bowles. In three games versus Todd Bowles' Tampa Bay defense, Rodgers has a losing record and has looked extremely ordinary. The four-time NFL MVP has wracked up just five touchdowns and he's also tossed four interceptions. The backdrop is laid out much differently for the 2026 edition, Rodgers has a new team, a new (his old) coach, is playing at a completely different level (which may actually further favor Bowles), and Bowles does not have nearly the same defensive firepower he once did. Sunday, will likely be the last time the two battle— A final chapter in the story. The storylines for Sunday's Bowles-Rodgers epilogue, can Todd Bowles get him again? Rodgers has yet to play a clean game against Bowles' Bucs. Will the Buccaneers' offense be able to stay mistake free for a second straight week? Turnovers, like they had against Rodgers' former team two weeks ago, will almost assuredly sink them into a self-dug 1-5 hole.

away.blurb: Wilson had no catches on one target before exiting in the second quarter of the 34-22 win. He was grabbing his left hand after an incompletion and did not return to the game. ESPN reported that Wilson is still gathering more information about the injury and will seek a second opinion. Wilson, a third-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft by Pittsburgh, has 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns in five games this season. The 25-year-old has 26 receptions for 354 yards and four TDs over the last two seasons for the Steelers. Wilson’s status comes after Pittsburgh placed wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on injured reserve Saturday and Ben Skowronek also left Sunday’s game with a calf injury. away.headline: Steelers injury report: Pittsburgh enters road trip with abundance of injuries
away.blurb: Out of the bye, road trips to face the division rival Bengals and in-state rival Eagles await. Neither is a long trip in terms of mileage, but the Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since 1965, and it follows an AFC North dogfight. The receivers room is the most pressing problem. Pittman will be out for at least the next three games after being placed on injured reserve. The veteran was a key offseason acquisition but has only played in three games in which he’s caught seven passes for 89 yards. The extent of the injuries to Wilson and Skowronek, sustained against Indianapolis, are not yet known, but McCarthy said Monday that both will be out for at least the Tampa Bay game. The secondary is a bit better off. Ramsey spent the week leading up to the Colts game on the injury report but handled a normal workload. Only Dean was absent, and the Steelers have not yet taken the step of adding the free agent cornerback signing to injured reserve. Dean was a limited practice participant Wednesday while Ramsey was out with a wrist injury listed. McCarthy hinted strongly that Dowdle is expected back this week from the toe injury he sustained in Week 2 against New England. He was also limited Wednesday. That should help the offense manage the reps of Jaylen Warren, who’s handled a heavy workload in Dowdle’s absence. First-year coach Mike McCarthy’s team will play four of its next five games on the road starting this week, and it will take multiple longer – and daunting – trips to do so before things begin to moderate in the back half of the 2026 schedule. All of it will unfold amid mounting absences. Running back Rico Dowdle; receivers Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek; and defensive backs Jamel Dean and Jalen Ramsey have all been hurt in some form or fashion recently. The stretch will be one of, if not the, most grueling in the franchise’s history and could determine whether the Steelers ’ 3-2 start has legs, or whether another mediocre year awaits a franchise that hasn’t won an NFL playoff game since 2017. NFL Week 6 brings a road trip to Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers . That’s a 1,000-or-so-mile trip right off the bat against a desperate 1-4 team that needs a win to preserve any postseason hopes. One week later, the Steelers will board a long flight to Paris to face the New Orleans Saints in the first NFL regular season game in France. It will be only the second international game for Pittsburgh since 2013. It picked up a win against Minnesota in Dublin, Ireland last October, but the travel schedule was much kinder surrounding that date. The Steelers got to enjoy a bye after their trip to the Emerald Isle and did not need to travel any further than Massachusetts until they visited the Los Angeles Chargers in early November. It was a similar story when they played in London13 years ago. They came home to a bye, and most travel was relatively local for the month before and after. Los Angeles enters the game at 2-3 after a heartbreaking 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night. Arizona is 1-4 and coming off a disappointing 45-21 defeat against the Detroit Lions. Both teams need a strong performance, making Sunday's divisional matchup an important opportunity to build momentum. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. Matthew Stafford Leads the Rams Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford will be a major factor in Sunday's game as Los Angeles looks to rebound from its difficult loss to Buffalo. Stafford has thrown for 1,572 yards and nine touchdowns through five games, establishing himself as the centerpiece of an offense capable of producing explosive plays. However, six interceptions have created problems, and protecting the football will be important against Arizona. Head coach Sean McVay will look to get the offense back on track by utilizing his talented group of playmakers. Wide receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams give Stafford two dangerous options in the passing game, while running back Kyren Williams provides balance on the ground. Williams has recorded 343 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns, making him an important part of Los Angeles' offensive attack. The Rams will also need to adjust along the offensive line, with left tackle Alaric Jackson suspended for Sunday's matchup. Jacoby Brissett Looks to Keep Arizona Competitive Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett will lead the Cardinals as they attempt to bounce back from their loss to Detroit. Brissett has thrown for 1,110 yards and nine touchdowns this season. Despite Arizona's struggles, he has shown the ability to move the football through the air and keep the offense competitive. Tight end Trey McBride remains one of his most reliable targets, entering the matchup with 42 receptions for 308 yards and three touchdowns. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love has also contributed to Arizona's offense, although his availability and workload will be worth monitoring after he missed practice Wednesday with an ankle issue. First-year head coach Mike LaFleur will need his offense to produce consistently against a Rams defense looking to force turnovers and create pressure. A Crucial NFC West Matchup Sunday's game gives Los Angeles an opportunity to recover from its overtime defeat and improve its record. Arizona needs a stronger defensive performance after allowing 45 points against Detroit. With Stafford leading an explosive passing attack and Brissett looking to keep the Cardinals competitive, both quarterbacks will face important challenges. The Rams and Cardinals have plenty to prove, and Sunday's matchup could be an important moment for both teams as the NFC West race continues.

Conveniently, the Cardinals are coming to town. Los Angeles has spent enough time trading punches with contenders. Now Matthew Stafford gets an Arizona defense that should provide a much friendlier afternoon, even with the shortened turnaround after Monday night. The Cardinals can move the ball through Trey McBride and Michael Wilson, and Jeremiyah Love gives the offense a reason to stay patient. I just don't see enough defensive resistance to keep the Rams from eventually creating separation, especially after the way they fell to the Bills . away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their first injury report of Week 5.
