It appeared that LaFleur claimed Williams would be unavailable for Sunday’s game when he said, “He’s not going to clear the concussion protocol.” The report is an estimate because the Rams did not practice after playing the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. home.headline: Rams Move Closer to Getting Keagen Trost Back Following Alaric Jackson Suspension
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams have officially opened rookie offensive lineman Keagen Trost’s practice window ahead of Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals. If all goes well, the plan is to activate Trost from injured reserve and have him available against Arizona. Head coach Sean McVay noted on Tuesday that the plan would be for David Quessenberry to start in Jackson’s place. However, given the lack of depth at tackle, McVay also said that the team would look into opening Trost’s practice window with the expectation that he would be available against the Cardinals. “‘DQ’ will take that spot. Then that'll also open up the opportunity for us to start Trost’s clock with the expectation of him being back out there this week,” said McVay on Tuesday. McVay added on Thursday that as long as Trost is feeling good, the Rams expect him to be available for Sunday’s game. The team will also be mindful of not putting him in a situation that isn’t good for his development, given how long it’s been since Trost played. The Rams drafted Trost in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Trost had a good summer, playing with the first- and second-team offenses at multiple positions. During the first preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs, Trost hurt his hamstring. Prior to roster cutdowns, the Rams put Trost on injured reserve to keep another roster spot available. “It’s not too big for him. He’s a very mature rookie,” said McVay last week on the Coach McVay show . “Got the ability to play on both the left and right side. Probably a little bit more comfortable on the right, but certainly you see the athleticism, the flexibility to get in and out of right- and-left handed stances. I like what he’s about and think he’s got a bright future for us.” While Justin Dedich remains on injured reserve, it makes sense that the Rams are prioritizing Trost given the need at tackle. Dedich can only play on the interior, while Trost is more of a tackle who can move inside. If the Rams were to need depth on the interior, Dedich would be an option.For now, the Rams are moving toward activating Trost from injured reserve. The Rams haven’t gotten much production out of their rookie class this season. While Trost will likely serve as Quessenberry’s backup on Sunday, his return will provide much-needed depth at tackle. On Tuesday, the NFL announced that Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson would be suspended for the next two games . Jackson was caught on camera throwing a punch at Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb following Monday night’s loss. After an appeal, Jackson’s suspension was reduced to just one game. During training camp, the Rams seemed pleased with Trost. While he’s more comfortable on the right side, McVay has talked about his ability to play on the left if needed. Trost can also slide in at guard. home.headline: Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams
home.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. "I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued. "Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered." Has Love lost any of his explosiveness? "You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital." Kansas City is 4-0 after its bye, while Los Angeles is 0-5 following a 23-17 loss to Denver. Kickoff at Arrowhead Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. The Chiefs are favored by 8.5 points, but a routine favorite winning comfortably would hardly qualify as a bold prediction. Instead, this forecast projects an exceptional rushing performance, an unexpected Chargers defensive highlight and a fourth-quarter rally that changes the complexion of the afternoon without changing the winner. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 200 yards and three touchdowns Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Walker has already accumulated 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 87 carries through four games. That translates to more than six yards per attempt, giving Kansas City a foundation for dominating without asking Patrick Mahomes to carry every possession. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Chiefs average 6.5 yards per offensive play compared with the Chargers' 4.8. Their third-down conversion rate is also substantially better: 44% against 34.85%. Those advantages can sustain drives and produce the repeated rushing opportunities necessary for a monster individual afternoon. The prediction goes beyond another efficient outing. Walker reaches 200 rushing yards for the game and scores three times, becoming the central reason Kansas City controls possession and repeatedly finishes drives. There is an important limitation: Los Angeles allows only 5.0 yards per play, the same figure as Kansas City. This is not a forecast built on pretending the Chargers cannot defend. It depends on Walker maintaining his explosiveness while the Chiefs create an unusually favorable game script. If Kansas City builds an early advantage, sustained rushing volume can turn Walker's strong start into the biggest performance of his season. The Chargers intercept Patrick Mahomes twice, including a pick-six Mahomes has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions through four games, with a 106.2 passer rating. Predicting two interceptions in one afternoon means Los Angeles matches his entire season total, despite entering winless. The statistical route to that surprise exists. The Chargers allow opponents to convert just 31.25% of third downs, compared with Kansas City's 37.04%. Forcing longer, obvious passing situations could provide opportunities that disappear when Walker keeps the offense ahead of schedule. Los Angeles needs more than ordinary defensive stops because its offense averages just 16.8 points per game. A defensive touchdown would change both field position and scoreboard pressure without requiring Justin Herbert to repeatedly rescue stalled possessions. The call is that one aggressive coverage read becomes an interception return for a touchdown, while another takeaway interrupts a promising Chiefs drive. That would be an unexpected blemish on Mahomes' efficient opening month. It would also illustrate why a team's record does not eliminate its capacity to produce a game-changing individual moment. Justin Herbert leads a 17-point fourth quarter, but Kansas City survives Herbert's current numbers make this the most counterintuitive offensive prediction: 937 passing yards, five touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 70.2 passer rating through five games. He has also absorbed 17 sacks. Against Denver, he managed 121 passing yards and was sacked five times. Receiving availability remains uncertain after Ladd McConkey dressed without playing, Quentin Johnston missed the game and Tre' Harris suffered a hamstring injury. Nevertheless, the prediction is that Herbert finally finds rhythm against a defense protecting a substantial lead. Two touchdown drives and a field goal produce 17 fourth-quarter points, forcing Kansas City to finish the game with its offense rather than coast. Walker provides that answer. The final forecast is Chiefs 38, Chargers 31: Kansas City remains unbeaten, but Los Angeles delivers a much stronger response than its record suggests. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Kansas City, but divisional familiarity and turnovers can make a comfortable matchup unpredictable. Kansas City enters the game at 4-0 after winning its first four contests, while Los Angeles is searching for its first victory after opening the season 0-5. The Chargers will have a difficult challenge at Arrowhead Stadium as they try to turn their season around against one of the AFC's early standouts. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. Eastern on CBS. Patrick Mahomes Leads the Chiefs Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has helped Kansas City get off to an impressive start in 2026. Through four games, Mahomes has thrown for 1,037 yards and nine touchdowns with just two interceptions, giving the Chiefs a productive passing attack. Kansas City has also found success on the ground with running back Kenneth Walker III. Walker has rushed for 537 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 6.2 yards per carry. His ability to produce explosive runs has given opposing defenses another major concern beyond Mahomes. Head coach Andy Reid will look to keep that offensive balance going against a Chargers defense that has shown the ability to pressure quarterbacks. The Chiefs will also monitor wide receiver Rashee Rice, who missed practice Wednesday with a hamstring injury. Justin Herbert Faces a Difficult Challenge For Los Angeles, quarterback Justin Herbert needs to help an offense that has struggled to produce consistently. Herbert has thrown for 937 yards, five touchdowns and seven interceptions through five games. The Chargers have averaged only 16.8 points per game, making offensive improvement a major priority. Herbert has the arm talent to challenge Kansas City's secondary, but he will need better protection and consistent production from his receiving corps. Injuries have complicated that task, with several Los Angeles wide receivers and defensive starters appearing on the team's injury report this week. Head coach Jim Harbaugh must find a way to help his team limit mistakes and sustain drives. A stronger running game could ease the pressure on Herbert and help keep Mahomes off the field. Andy Reid vs. Jim Harbaugh The coaching matchup adds another layer to this divisional rivalry. Reid has Kansas City playing efficient football on both sides of the ball, while Harbaugh is trying to find answers after a difficult opening month. The Chargers swept the Chiefs in 2025, adding extra motivation for Kansas City to protect its home field and maintain control of the AFC West rivalry. A Critical AFC West Matchup Kansas City has an opportunity to improve to 5-0 and continue building momentum after its bye week. Los Angeles, meanwhile, needs a complete performance to avoid falling further behind in the division. Mahomes and Walker give the Chiefs multiple ways to attack, while Herbert will need to deliver a more consistent performance to help the Chargers compete. With the Chiefs chasing another strong start and the Chargers desperate to get their season moving, Sunday's matchup carries plenty of importance for both teams.

home.headline: NFL insider reveals latest injury update for Chiefs WR Rashee Rice
home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs may be without star wide receiver Rashee Rice in their Week 6 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers this weekend. After sustaining a hamstring injury during Kansas City's win over the Las Vegas Raiders on October 4, Rice has now missed the Chiefs' first two practice sessions for Week 6 — which officially put the veteran pass-catcher's status in question. NFL insider Adam Schefter revealed the latest injury update for Rice in a post to his official Twitter account on October 14, just days before Kansas City is set to face the Chargers in a rivalry matchup at Arrowhead Stadium: While Rice could hypothetically take the field to face the Chargers this weekend despite his injury, Kansas City's coaching staff is likely to be cautious with their injured wideout, especially after speedy receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a serious lower-body injury in Week 4 that may prove to be a season-ender. home.blurb: Chiefs-Chargers Week 6 Thursday injury report: Peter Woods limited - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Chiefs-Chargers Week 6 Thursday injury report: Peter Woods limited Left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) was a limited participant in practice again, marking the 2025 first-round pick's second time on the practice field since the team was in training camp. For more about Simmons, here are Reid's comments from Wednesday . Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods (Neck) was added to the injury report Thursday as a limited participant in practice. Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (Knee) was a limited participant in practice. His time on the field is regularly managed due to a lingering knee issue. Tackle Joe Alt (neck), guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), wide receiver Tre' Harris (hamstring), cornerback Donte Jackson (hamstring), and safety Derwin James (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday. Pass rusher Khalil Mack sat on Wednesday, but he returned from the rest day on Thursday. Outside linebacker Bud Dupree (NIR – Rest) did not practice on Thursday after limited participation on Wednesday due to a neck injury. Cornerback Rodney Shelley (Hamstring) did not practice on Thursday after limited participation on Wednesday. Alt, Awosika, Jackson and James all missed the Chargers' Week 5 contest against the Denver Broncos . Harris left during the game with a hamstring injury and did not return. Defensive tackle Jamaree Caldwell (knee), defensive tackle Justin Egoigbe (shoulder), linebacker Daiyan Henley (knee), wide receiver Quentin Johnston (chest), wide receiver KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring), wide receiver Ladd McConkey (foot), defensive back Elijah Molden (hamstring), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad), defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson (hamstring) and safety Kendall Williamson (ankle) were limited on both days. Johnston and Thompson did not play against Denver. McConkey was nominally active on Sunday, but he did not enter the game against the Broncos. Lambert-Smith is on Los Angeles' Reserve/Injured list but has been designated to return. picks.blurb: NFL Week 6 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Another Packers-Cowboys clash, Raiders scare Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Jordan Love | GettyImages | Illustration by Michael Castillo Cody Williams Tue, October 13, 2026 at 5:54 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The unbeatable Los Angeles Rams superteam is now 2-3 on the 2026 NFL season. The Houston Texans just got their first win. The Dallas Cowboys can't get out of their own way, and the Buffalo Bills are mauling everyone in their way. It's been a wacky start to the season, which has made our NFL picks and predictions for every game each week a bit more difficult than I expected. We're having to adjust our perceptions and expectations on the fly, and we're still in the mix as we head into what should be a fascinating Week 6. Zach Rotman came out of the bullpen for me last week and came through with a solid week. Many, many thanks to him for helping the cause, but I'm back in the saddle now. Let's hope I don't make this thing go any further off the rails, but let's dive right into this fun slate with our NFL picks for Week 6 as we make predictions both straight-up and against the spread for all 14 games on the slate this week. NFL Week 6 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game NFL Week 6 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Seahawks vs. Broncos (TNF) Seahawks -2.5 Texans vs. Jaguars (London) Bears vs. Falcons Ravens vs. Browns Jets vs. Patriots Patriots -7.5 Saints vs. Giants Titans vs. Colts Panthers vs. Eagles Panthers +1.5 Steelers vs. Buccaneers Steelers -2.5 Cardinals vs. Rams Bills vs. Raiders Chargers vs. Chiefs Cowboys vs. Packers Commanders vs. 49ers 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 51-28 (Last week 9-6) | ATS Record: 37-40-2 (Last week 8-7) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 6 prediction to make Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders (+5.5) The Buffalo Bills have been rolling, including toppling the Rams in overtime in Los Angeles on Monday night. Stop me if you've heard this one before, but Buffalo has one of the NFL's best offenses behind Josh Allen and it doesn't seem like there's a defense in the league that's going to be able to stop this team from scoring 30 points - they're quite literally averaging 32.7 points per game after the first five games of the year. Meanwhile, the Raiders have certainly fallen back to earth a bit, losing two straight after their 3-0 start to the season. At the same time, the Bills defense is the same problem it's been for the past few years. It seems like Buffalo has to produce at this level offensively to win games because the defense is going to give it up. While the Raiders might not be a surprise contender, they still look like a quite competent football team behind Kirk Cousins and, while Buffalo will be able to score on their defense, they're still averaging 26.4 points per game on the year. I think Buffalo still has the offensive firepower against a middling defense to get the win in this game. But with it being in Vegas against a team that has a legitimate pulse, it's going to be another shootout and one that could likely be decided by a field goal once again. 5.5 points is a bit too many, so we'll take the Raiders against the spread and pray. Easiest NFL Week 6 pick on the board Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs (-8.5) This line could've been two touchdowns and I'm still taking the Kansas City Chiefs over the division rival Chargers. For starters, what has LA shown this season to make you believe they have a chance in Arrowhead in Week 6? No, seriously. There's been little evidence to think that this game will be close as the Chiefs have been absolutely rolling on both sides of the ball while Justin Herbert delivers the worst season of his career, the Chargers defense is middling at its best and the self-inflicted wounds in each game from LA multiply likes the heads of a hydra. If that weren't enough, Andy Reid is famously one of the most lethal head coaches when his team is coming off of the bye week. This isn't to say that the Chiefs are a perfect team as I maintain that they still need to find some more upgrades at wide receiver, especially after the gnarly Tyquan Thornton injury. While that may be true, though, they are a far better coached and more talented team than the winless Chargers and I wouldn't be surprised if this game was lopsided and out of hand early in favor of the home side. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas Cowboys (+1.5) at Green Bay Packers Coming off of a home loss to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels and the previously winless Buccaneers, naturally I'm taking the Dallas Cowboys to go on the road to Lambeau and beat the Packers as underdogs. What about this doesn't make sense to you? Yes, the optics look strange. However, this isn't about expecting the Cowboys hiring Mike Pettine to essentially help out new defensive coordinator Christian Parker drastically improving the defense, though it can't hurt. It's more about this being a likely shootout between these two teams because, despite what happened to Tyson Bagent and the Bears, I still don't trust Green Bay on that side of the ball. Furthermore, I also still don't trust the Packers run game, even against Dallas. Expect this game to go back and forth throughout the action, but I believe the Cowboys are going to have more offensive firepower and some adjustments on the side of the ball you can actually trust Dallas on to attack Green Bay throughout. They might not come up with many stops of their own, but they'll have enough to pull out the win. Plus, just from a narrative perspective, if ever there was a time for the Cowboys to keep their fans from abandoning ship, it's a game like this, and this franchise has been masterful at doing exactly that over the years. picks.headline: Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6
picks.blurb: Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 Tim Crean, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:44 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Buffalo Bills face off against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. This matchup between the 4-1 Bills and the 3-2 Raiders gets a prime spot in the late Sunday window as one of the best games of the week. These two original AFC franchises haven't played a game with meaningful stakes for both teams since the 1993 "Just Freeze Baby" Divisional Round game . Now, as both sides come into this game with winning records, let's make some bold Bills-Raiders predictions. Start your Raiders in fantasy football The Bills are their own worst enemy so far this season, as they love to gift their opponents chances to stay in the game. Whether it is shockingly cavalier Josh Allen interceptions, infuriating James Cook fumbles, or the fact that the defense (outside of Deone Walker and Gregory Rousseau) looks like it has no clue what it is doing right now, Buffalo loves keeping the other team in the game. Sunday will be no different, as fans should expect at least two turnovers from the Bills' offense and long stretches where the Raiders' O looks like the 2007 New England Patriots. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That means big games from the Raiders' defense, Kirk Cousins, Brock Bowers, Ashton Jeanty, and maybe even the likes of Mike Washington Jr., Michael Mayer, and Tre Tucker. So, for all you fantasy football players out there, any Raiders on your roster should be a good play in Week 6 . Josh Allen delivers again Despite the mediocre (or worse) play at times from the Bills' offensive line, wide receivers, tight end, and running backs, and defensive back seven, the Bills are 4-1 and leading the AFC East thanks to one man: Brandon Beane. Just kidding! He's the reason the rest of the team is struggling so much. The real reason is Josh Allen. Through five weeks, Allen is still the betting favorite for NFL MVP this year. Yes, Brock Bowers is playing great, and Patrick Mahomes is back, but if you define MVP as the players whose absence would tank his team's chances the most, Allen has to be the answer. Monday night's dramatic OT win over the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams came courtesy of 210 yards passing and a staggering 121 yards rushing from the Bills QB. Sure, he threw his obligatory head-scratching pick in the first half, but in the second, it was a one-man battle with 53 Rams players, and the singular man won. Against the Raiders, expect more of the same. Vegas has an improved defense this season and an incredible pass rusher in Maxx Crosby, but that only means Allen will be forced to take off even more as usual. And with his receivers getting minimal separation and Cook's suspect ball security, it will be all Allen, all the time in Week 6. Bills 31, Raiders 24 This won't be a cakewalk for the Bills by any means, as the Raiders are one of (if not) the most improved teams in the league. We know Cousins is a professional QB, the Raiders have some incredible young offensive weapons, and Klint Kubiak seems like a legit NFL head coach with an incredibly bright future. Allen doesn't have those last two things, as his skill position core is the exact same as last year, as long as D.J. Moore is out injured and his "new" head coach is just the same offensive coordinator who couldn't get it done the past three seasons, but with a more impressive title. Nevertheless, Allen should be able to will his Bills to victory over the Raiders in Week 6 just by sheer force of talent and will. As good as Las Vegas has looked at times this season, they are probably a year or two away from being legit contenders. That's why we'll take the Buffalo to win here, and to do so by slightly more than the -5.5-point spread suggests. picks.headline: Bills vs. Raiders Preview: Buffalo Looks to Keep Rolling Against Las Vegas
picks.blurb: Bills vs. Raiders Preview: Buffalo Looks to Keep Rolling Against Las Vegas - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search News Finance More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Scores / Schedules Bills vs. Raiders Preview: Buffalo Looks to Keep Rolling Against Las Vegas Photo by: Bob DeChiara Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 8:31 p.m. UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads About our Ads The Buffalo Bills head to Las Vegas on Sunday for a Week 6 matchup against the Raiders, with both teams looking to strengthen their positions in the AFC playoff race. Buffalo enters the game at 4-1 after an exciting 37-34 overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night. The Raiders, meanwhile, are 3-2 after suffering a 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots. With the Bills carrying one of the league's most productive offenses and Las Vegas looking to bounce back, Sunday's matchup at Allegiant Stadium presents an important test for both teams. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. Eastern on CBS. Josh Allen Leads Buffalo's Explosive Offense Quarterback Josh Allen remains the centerpiece of Buffalo's offense. Through five games, Allen has thrown for 1,249 yards and seven touchdowns while adding eight rushing touchdowns. His ability to create plays with both his arm and legs makes him one of the most difficult quarterbacks to defend. Allen was particularly dangerous against the Rams, throwing for 342 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for 121 yards. His performance helped Buffalo survive a back-and-forth contest and improve to 4-1. Running back James Cook has also been productive, rushing for 532 yards through five games. His speed and ability to create explosive plays give the Bills another weapon that Las Vegas must account for. Head coach Joe Brady will look to keep the offense balanced while helping Allen avoid costly turnovers. Buffalo has committed nine giveaways over its last three games, making ball security an important focus heading into Sunday. Raiders Need a Strong Response Las Vegas will look to quarterback Kirk Cousins to help the offense recover from its disappointing performance against New England. Cousins has thrown for 1,269 yards and 12 touchdowns through five games, giving the Raiders a capable passing attack. Tight end Brock Bowers has been one of Cousins' primary targets, recording 312 receiving yards and three touchdowns. His ability to create mismatches could be especially important against a Buffalo defense that has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks. The Raiders will also rely on running back Ashton Jeanty , who has rushed for 291 yards this season. Establishing the ground game could help Las Vegas control possession and prevent Allen from spending too much time on the field. Head coach Klint Kubiak will need his team to improve its offensive line play and limit mistakes after the loss to New England. A Major Test for Both Teams Buffalo enters the matchup averaging 32.8 points per game, while Las Vegas has averaged 26.4. Both defenses have experienced difficulties, creating opportunities for the offenses to make an impact. The Bills will try to maintain their momentum after the overtime win, while the Raiders need a response at home to remain competitive in the AFC West. With Allen's dual threat ability, Cousins' passing production and two offenses looking to establish control, Sunday's matchup could be an important measuring stick for both teams as the NFL season continues.

Buffalo is coming off its most impressive win of the season, beating the potent Los Angeles Rams in overtime, 37-34, in a Monday Night Football classic where win probabilities swung to and fro like the doors of an Old West saloon. The Raiders come into the game after a 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots led by QB Drake Maye. Even with the short week, Josh Allen and the Bills are the early favorites among NFL analysts. away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams came into the season looking like one of the dominant teams in the NFL, one that would have an excellent chance of contending for a Super Bowl title. In addition to the outstanding offensive combination of quarterback Matthew Stafford and wide out Puka Nacua, the Rams appeared to have put together one of the dangerous defensive teams in recent memory. The Rams had acquired Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in the offseason, and bringing in the best defensive player in the league got the attention of Aaron Donald . The former All-Pro defensive tackle had retired after the 2023 season, but he sensed the addition of Garrett made the Rams a powerful team with the capability of dominating opponents. Donald was interested in making a comeback and after flirting with the idea throughout training camp, he decided to return to the Rams shortly before the start fo the season. The Rams are expected to have nearly all of their top players available for the test against the Bills. Here's the way the latest injury report looked after the team's last practice session: TE Colby Parkinson, full participation in practice (knee), OLB Byron Young, did not practice (rest), OL Alaric Jackson, did not practice (rest), TE Tyler Higbee, did not practice (rest), WR Davante Adams, full participation in practice (rest), LB Nathan Landman, full participation in practice (shoulder), S Quentin Lake, questionable (hip), OLB Josaiah Stewart, limited participation in practice (groin), LB Grant Stuard, limited participation in practice (hamstring). "He was questionable to play Sunday and only got cleared after a nine-minute pregame workout and discussion with team trainers and coaches. But keep an eye on this situation. The Raiders have internally discussed giving Jeanty a week off to heal at some point." Jeanty was limited to 27 yards on 10 carries in Sunday's 45-17 blowout loss to the New England Patriots, though he added 50 receiving yards on three catches. He hasn't rushed for 60 yards or more since his 102-yard performance in Week 1 against the Miami Dolphins, and he hasn't reached the end zone since his two receiving touchdowns in that same game. If Jeanty is forced to sit out at any point, Graziano noted that the Raiders "have confidence in rookie running back Mike Washington Jr.'s ability to hold things down for a game or two with Dylan Laube backing him up, if it came to that." Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty has been off to a disappointing start to the 2026 season, and it sounds like he could need some time to rest. While Dallas is coming off an embarrassing performance , the Packers are coming off a blowout win over the Chicago Bears. Common sense would tell you that the Packers would be favored considering their outcome, but the oddsmakers appear to have something else in mind. When the opening odds were released late Sunday night, it was actually the Cowboys entering the week as 1.5-point favorites on the road at Lambeau Field . With Dallas having extra rest and motivation, and the Packers coming off a divisional win, it sets up as a perfect trap game for the Cowboys to steal on the road. This week, the Cowboys will head to Green Bay to face the Packers on Sunday night . Dallas spent the week looking for defensive solutions after a rough Week 5 showing against the Buccaneers. Can Dallas' defense survive a key test from Jordan Love and the Packers' offense? The Dallas Morning News' columnists and beat writers offered up their predictions for the Week 6 matchup at Lambeau Field below: Tim Cowlishaw Cowboys do not have a rich history at Lambeau Field (or against the Packers at home, for that matter) but Dallas' ability to run the ball on Green Bay should keep this game interesting into the fourth quarter. Atlanta ran for 242 yards at Lambeau weeks ago. The scary part for Dallas is that Jordan Love is coming off a 367-yard passing day against Chicago and licking his chops while looking at the only defense yet to intercept a pass this season. Joey Porter Jr. to the rescue? Maybe not. Packers 26, Cowboys 20 Good news, Cowboys fans: I've been wrong on most of my Cowboys game predictions this year, so there's hope! But seriously: this team keeps us on our toes, especially after losing last week to Tampa Bay . I foresee another close loss to Green Bay. Packers 31, Cowboys 28 In the last seven meetings between these teams, the winner has scored more than 30 points. That includes last season's 40-40 tie at AT&T Stadium . The Cowboys are just as lost on defense as last season, if not more, so expect another high-scoring game. You never know what you're going to get with these Cowboys, but it's difficult to see them coming out on top Sunday night. They'll have to play a perfect game on offense. Packers 38, Cowboys 34 Abraham Nudelstejer The Cowboys' best chance to beat the Packers is to turn this into a shootout. Even then, it's difficult to envision Dallas' defense coming up with the late stop needed to secure a victory. The Cowboys' defense remains the team's biggest weakness and a major reason it continues to tread water in the mediocre NFC East. If Dak Prescott fails to match Jordan Love score for score, Dallas could find itself in trouble early and chasing the game all night. Packers 34, Cowboys 20 Kevin Sherrington Now that Jerry Jones has officially signaled that Christian Parker isn't yet who they thought he was and this is going to take longer than he'd hoped, let's officially put to bed any crazy predictions from yours truly that an NFC title game run is in the offing. The Cowboys will be lucky to win nine games. This won't be one of them. Packers 30, Cowboys 27 Calvin Watkins All the defensive moves by the Cowboys this week won't help against the Packers. The defense has trouble stopping people, and do you believe Christian Watson and Matthew Golden will be slowed down by the Cowboys' secondary? The Cowboys will need big games from CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens to make this a contest. The run game has to show up, too. picks.blurb: Week 6 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys and Packers had much different results last week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 15, 2026 at 2:37 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One week can change the entire perception of an NFL team — sometimes that's good, sometimes it's not. The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers were both 2-2 coming into last week's games. The Cowboys weren't considered a Super Bowl contender, but they were at least looking OK — especially in a bad NFC East — with a home game against the winless Buccaneers coming up. The Packers had played so poorly through four weeks that they were home underdogs to the Bears for the first time in 20 years , even though Chicago was starting its backup quarterback. The Cowboys and Packers come into Week 6's Sunday night game with their seasons flipped around. The Cowboys looked horrible against the Buccaneers, losing to an undrafted rookie quarterback in Jalon Daniels. The defensive problems finally got to a point in which the Cowboys hired longtime NFL defensive coordinator Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant and said defensive coordinator Christian Parker will now call plays from the press box. There's always some angst in Dallas because of the attention on the Cowboys all the time, but it's not like the defensive problems are made up. Dallas was last in defensive DVOA last season and they're last so far this season. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Meanwhile, the talk of Matt LaFleur being on the hot seat seems like it was a lot longer than a week ago. The best way to gain back the confidence of Packers fans is to blow out the Bears, and the Packers did just that. They blasted Chicago, 31-7, with Jordan Love embarrassing the Bears defense with his deep passing and Green Bay shutting down everything Chicago's offense wanted to do. After not playing a good game through four weeks, the Packers played a great game in Week 5. That makes Week 6 hard to figure out. Do the Cowboys rebound or is the defense simply unfixable? What's the real Packers team — the one that couldn't run the ball, couldn't protect Love and had a below-average defense through four games, or the one we saw Sunday? The Packers are small favorites Sunday night, indicating the oddsmakers don't have a lot of confidence in them still. But it's tougher to bank on the Cowboys' defense. Packers -1.5 is the pick , though it could all look different for both teams next week. That's how the NFL goes. The Green Bay Packers' MarShawn Lloyd celebrates a touchdown with the fans at Lambeau Field last week. (AP Photo/Nam Huh) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 6 of the NFL season: Seahawks (-2.5) over Broncos Not all is great for the defending champs, who can't run the ball and still don't have an offensive option other than Jaxon Smith-Njigba. But they've been far better than the Broncos, who were on their way to losing to the winless and injury-plagued Chargers before saving themselves with a fourth-quarter rally. The matchup of Seattle's defense against an aimless Broncos offense is enough to take the Seahawks. Jaguars (-2.5) over Texans A bit of a weird line. The Jaguars are 4-1 and while last week's miracle win over the Eagles wasn't great, they do look like a legitimate contender in the AFC. The Texans are 1-4 and their lone win came against the 0-5 Titans. And yet, in a neutral site game — if either team has the edge it's Jacksonville, who does the London trip every season and stayed overseas after playing there last week — the Jaguars aren't even giving a full field goal. Yes it's a desperate Houston team with a very good defense, but it's not a lot of respect for the Jaguars. Falcons (+1.5) over Bears It appears Michael Penix Jr. and Caleb Williams will start, which should make for an entertaining game. The big question for this one will be what to make of the Bears defense. In Week 1 and 5 they gave up 68 combined points. From Weeks 2-4 they allowed 28 points. The hot stretch in the middle could have come from facing three bad offenses (Vikings without Kyler Murray in bad weather, Eagles, Jets) instead of the Panthers and Packers, their other two opponents who both scored more than 30 points. The Falcons are a good offense with Penix, so points should be coming. Browns (+5.5) over Ravens The Ravens should have confidence after beating the Falcons without Lamar Jackson last week. However, a Tyler Huntley offense still isn't one I'm comfortable laying 5.5 points with on the road. Buccaneers (+2.5) over Steelers Metrics like DVOA and net EPA per play say these teams are practically even. The Buccaneers have the rest advantage, having played last Thursday night, and the Steelers are 0-2 on the road (3-0 at home). Daniels could be exposed by the best defense he's faced, but it's also not the intimidating Steelers defense from recent years. Patriots (-7.5) over Jets The Patriots are officially warmed up. The start to the season was lackluster, but Drake Maye is coming off two good games in a row. The Jets are better than some expected, but they're facing a team that has its season back on track and wants to keep that going. Bet the New England Patriots to cover the spread at sportsbooks Giants (+1.5) over Saints It's hard to buy the Giants. There's no evidence they're a good team despite their 3-1-1 record. But it's not like there are any signs that the Saints are much better. New Orleans is 30th in DVOA ahead of only the hopeless Titans and Dolphins. Anything can happen when Jameis Winston is starting at quarterback, good or bad — good luck predicting it. Panthers (-1) over Eagles It's weird to see the Panthers favored at Philadelphia (though some books have the Eagles as a small favorite). But to this point, Carolina has been the far better team. Also, they're coming off a bye while the Eagles come right off a flight from London, where they took a horrific loss after kicking a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left. Colts (-7) over Titans The Titans should be very happy the Dolphins exist, or else there would be even more talk about how bad they are. Indianapolis hasn't been great, either, but it's just too difficult to take the Titans right now. Cardinals (+12.5) over Rams It's quite possible the Rams take out their frustrations on the Cardinals. Los Angeles is 2-3, but the schedule has been tough and it starts to ease up with a game against Arizona, which just got throttled by the Lions. The Cardinals seem to be running out of steam after looking decent to start the season. Still, 12.5 points is a lot considering the Rams haven't looked great yet, and Arizona can move the ball, especially in garbage time. Raiders (+5.5) over Bills The Bills are coming off an emotional, difficult overtime win against the Rams on Monday night. They are the better team, but that's a tough situational spot, and the Raiders are not as bad as they looked last week against the Patriots. Let's give Vegas one more shot to show that 3-0 start wasn't fraudulent. Chiefs (-8) over Chargers The Chargers aren't just bad, they're injured. They held their own against the Broncos last week, but that probably says more about Denver. This season is already ugly for Los Angeles and it's not going to get much better. Commanders (+7.5) over 49ers If the Commanders aren't completely downtrodden after one of the dumbest endings in recent NFL history last week, in which they casually watched the final minute of overtime run out without getting a field-goal attempt, then this seems like too many points. The 49ers have played very well on both sides of the ball (the defense has been a great surprise), but there is some danger of a letdown after winning at Seattle. Take the points and hope last week's fiasco doesn't still linger for Washington. Last week: 5-9-1 Season to date: 34-43-2

away.headline: NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week
away.blurb: Now, to add insult to injury, the NFL is punishing two Cowboys players for their actions in Week 4 of the NFL season. Every weekend, the NFL sends out a report with its weekly punishments for holding players accountable for their actions during the prior week's games . NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week Anne Erickson Sat, October 10, 2026 at 9:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys fell 24-16 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on "Thursday Night Football" to kick off the NFL's Week 5 festivities, and it wasn't a good look for the franchise. The main reason this loss was rough is because the Cowboys fell to a 0-4 Buccaneers team that has undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels subbing for the injured Baker Mayfield. You know something is wrong when you're losing to an undrafted free agent, but in all seriousness, Daniels was impressive. So, it could be more about his impressive showing than the Cowboys tanking, but still, this franchise is already on the clock to turn things around this season. Two Cowboys players fined by the NFL "Player infractions may come to the league's attention in a variety of ways. The league may respond to an official's call during a game or to a specific play that a team submits for review," the league notes. In this weekend's report, the NFL slaps Cowboys player Reddy Steward with a $5,583 fine for unnecessary roughness due to a hit on a defenseless player at 10:57 in the third quarter, as well as Kavontae Turpin with an $11,941 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct due to taunting at 10:50 in the third quarter. So, it's just a bit more bad news for two guys playing for a franchise that's hurting. But it's still early in the season, so the Cowboys have lots of time to come back. away.headline: Dallas Cowboys Could Bench DaRon Bland to Avoid Paying Massive Injury Guarantees
away.blurb: As pointed out by ESPN's Bill Barnwell, the Cowboys would be in a frustrating financial hole if Bland were to suffer an injury this season. "The Cowboys don't want to be on the hook for that money, so it would hardly be a surprise if they took Bland out of the lineup altogether once (Cobie) Durant and (Joey) Porter Jr. are back on the field to avoid triggering those guarantees, which would happen if Bland suffers a significant injury," Barnwell wrote. The Cowboys are also still figuring out exactly what they have in Shavon Revel Jr., who impressed during training camp but has had his own share of struggles this season. From being a fifth-round pick to making NFL history, Dallas Cowboys cornerback DaRon Bland deserves a ton of credit for the career he's made for himself. However, the magic from his record-setting 2023 season has quickly faded. Despite signing a four-year, $90 million contract extension last August, Bland has become a liability this season on a Dallas defense that already has enough problems to deal with. Bland hasn't had an interception since Week 7 of last season. And if he's not jumping routes and running it back for a touchdown -- something he's done six times in his career -- Bland is getting burned down the field for huge gains. As a result of his fading production and hefty contract, the Cowboys face an interesting dilemma when it comes to how they handle Bland's involvement in the defense moving forward in order to help themselves both on the field and in the bank. Cowboys Would Owe DaRon Bland $13 Million Due to Injury Dallas would owe Bland $13 million in guaranteed money if he suffers "a significant injury." Should he stay healthy, the Cowboys would avoid having to pay up. This situation makes it perfectly reasonable for the Cowboys to bench Bland moving forward. Until he proves he can produce at the level that his contract commands, Dallas faces a lose-lose situation: continue to suffer on defense while running the risk of owing Bland millions in injury guarantees. If the Cowboys are going to be awful on defense, they might as well do it with cornerbacks that won't put them in a tough spot financially. Cowboys Have More Reasonable Options to Work With When everyone is healthy, Dallas has multiple options that certainly feel like an upgrade from the current version of Bland. The Cowboys signed former Los Angeles Rams cornerback Cobie Durant this season before making the blockbuster deal for former Pittsburgh Steelers star Joey Porter Jr. earlier this month. And on top of that, Dallas has versatile defensive back Caleb Downs, who brings a bit of everything as a slot corner or a safety. It's hard to imagine Bland being outright ruled inactive for Week 6's matchup against the Green Bay Packers but the Cowboys could certainly benefit by slowing decreasing his snap count as the season goes on. home.headline: Micah Parsons provides promising injury update for Packers fans
home.blurb: Micah Parsons, out since last December with a torn ACL, is nearing his comeback for the Packers as they look to bounce back from a slow start in the NFC North, winners of two games in a row. Around 9.5 months after his surgery last December, Parsons is nearing a return, but it won't come in Week 6 against his former Cowboys squad. He has yet to return to practice, and remains on Green Bay's PUP list as the team waits for him to be medically cleared. But it shouldn't be too long before that happens. "The biggest thing that people worried about with me, they're like, 'Man, why ain't he back yet?'" Parsons said. "If the Super Bowl was this week, I'm playing in the Super Bowl. But it's just about me making sure I have all the small things fixed first. What a lot of people don't figure out is it's not just the ACL. It's like, why did the ACL happen? What was weak? Because it all works together. It's a chain. And throughout the history of ACL, they notice if you come back early, there tends to be an overcompensation injury on the other side." Previously, he said he thought a return to face the Cowboys in Week 6 was "realistic," but it won't materialize as hoped. It won't be long before one of the NFL's premiere pass rushers is back on the field. Parsons provided the latest update on his timeline on his podcast recently, saying he's in the final stages of making sure his knee will hold up. Here's what Parsons said about his injury outlook. MORE: The Sporting News' latest 2027 NFL Mock Draft Micah Parsons provides injury update Parsons said on the latest episode of his podcast, "The Edge With Micah Parsons," that if it was a do-or-die game, he'd be ready to play, but has preferred to play it safe with his longer timeline. The star pass rusher said he wants to make sure he's fully at 100% before he returns. "It's like, what's the point of getting me back for four weeks and then next thing you know, my groin [is] bothering me," Parsons said. "So many people wanted me to be back for that game to make the game bigger than what it was," Parsons said on his podcast. "It's just another 'Sunday Night Football' game between two good teams. It's not about me. I think that probably let people down. 'Oh, Micah, he's gonna want to be back for the Dallas game.' No, I'm in that phase of life where I just want to be healthy again. That's it." For now, Parsons is waiting to be cleared so he can begin his ramp up to play. It won't be happening this week, but soon, the Packers will be getting a game-changing weapon back for their defense. picks.blurb: Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football Steven Bisig-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Wed, October 14, 2026 at 1:54 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads While the Washington Commanders are likely playing with a lame-duck coach, the San Francisco 49ers will be without a key defender. These teams, going in different directions, will meet in Week 6 on Monday Night Football, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Still reeling from a last-second overtime mental meltdown in the 27-27 tie to the Giants, the Commanders carry a record of 1-3-1 and a heavy underdog role into this game. Meanwhile, the 49ers are flying high with a record of 5-0 on the season. They're coming off an exciting 32-29 win over the Seahawks, giving them firm control of the NFC West title chase. 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 300 yards The Commanders have been good against the run this season, giving up only 95.4 yards per game. They will have a challenge against the 49ers' offense, who are No. 8 in rushing yards per game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Look for the Commanders to slow, not stop, Christian McCaffrey. However, that opens things up for the 49ers' passing attack to hit high gear. The biggest problem the Commanders will have is Mike Evans. That's not a deep analysis. It's something every team faces when playing the 49ers. Purdy said Evans makes a big difference , according to ESPN. "He's a game changer," Purdy said after the win over the Seahawks. "True X receiver that, if you get the right look and stuff and you give him a chance, he can make defenses pay. "I thought today he did a great job with that, going up and getting the ball multiple times and just using his length and everything to create some separation. So as a quarterback, any time I have an (opportunity) to go to him, it always feels good." Evans doesn't shy away from the attention. And why should he? He's a future Hall of Famer. "I do feel like I'm one of the best receivers in the game," Evans said. "I got a big frame, so if you throw it around me, I'm going to do my best to try to make those contested grabs." The 49ers won't have Deebo Samuel, who suffered a hamstring injury against the Seahawks. That could allow the Commanders to focus more attention on Evans. But the 49ers still have threats, including George Kittle. And even Kittle has major respect for Evans, according to a post on X. "Mike Evans is really good at football," Kittle posted. 49ers TE George Kittle will have a season-high reception total Kittle's best game came in Week 3 against the Cardinals as he grabbed six passes for 82 yards and a pair of scores. Look for him to have a similar line against the Commanders with Samuel on the shelf. The 49ers have Kittle, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, and Jacob Cowing on the roster. And that's enough , said head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to ESPN. "I think we have enough," Shanahan said. "We've got three guys on practice squad also who can help. I mean, anytime you lose this number of guys, whether it's four guys or five guys, whatever it is, it's a huge challenge. But we do have guys in this building who can do it, and we'll always look." Commanders QB Jayden Daniels will finally cross 200-yard passing mark In three games this season, Daniels hasn't totaled over 200 yards passing. Look for that to change against the 49ers. It makes sense for the 49ers to focus defensively on keeping Daniels in check as a runner. He's coming off a game where he ran for 103 yards on nine carries and a pair of touchdowns. And look for the Commanders' game plan to lean more on the passing game than it has so far this season. Part of it will likely be from necessity as the Commanders figure to be chasing points throughout this game. Daniels has a lot to prove after his late-game blunder against the Giants. He has tried to own the situation , according to ESPN. "We have to stop the clock," Daniels said. "We have to know the situation. We have to relay that as an offense. It starts with everyone, top down. Ultimately, it's on me." A bounce-back game against the 49ers by Daniels won't help Quinn's future as head coach. But it would be an olive branch to Commanders' fans who are furious about Daniels' mental meltdown. Commanders WR Terry McLaurin will get a long TD Look for the Commanders to strike deep against the 49ers. McLaurin should be the beneficiary with a 40-plus-yard score. McLaurin hasn't been anything special from a fantasy perspective this season. He had catch totals of 2, 2, 6, and 4 in his first four games. He has 203 total yards and one touchdown. Those aren't WR1 numbers. He is playing like a pedestrian blob so far this season. And while he probably won't juice up those numbers much against the 49ers' tough defense, it's not out of the realm of possibility for him to get a deep ball. How big of an ask is a 40-yard TD strike between Daniels and McLaurin? Consider that Daniels' longest pass of the season is 33 yards. McLaurin's longest catch is 30 yards. Those numbers seem to belie the likelihood of a long hookup. However, the 49ers can't fear the deep ball because of this duo's modest production. And that's why there's a window of opportunity for a bomb. However, look for the Commanders to fall to 1-4-1 after this one. They don't have the roster to compete with the 49ers. away.blurb: The Washington Commanders weren't finished making roster moves ahead of Sunday's game against the New York Giants. Saturday brought some help back to the defensive line, another option at receiver, and two players who won't be available after all. New York also made a few moves of its own, while Washington still has some problems to figure out before kickoff. Jefferson's elevation is particularly interesting with Stefon Diggs already ruled out and Terry McLaurin questionable with a hamstring injury. Washington also downgraded cornerback Trey Amos and running back Jeremy McNichols to OUT, ending any possibility of either making his return Sunday. New York also elevated receiver Dalen Cambre and outside linebacker Trace Ford from its practice squad. To understand how important Lucas Patrick is now, you have to understand that the Washington Commanders spent the entire offseason trying to convince anyone who asked that Nick Allegretti was the team's center after abruptly releasing Tyler Biadasz. Commanders GM Adam Peters insisted Allegretti was their guy until training camp, when Allegretti went down with a calf strain and stayed out. away.blurb: Commanders vs. Giants Friday injury report: Stefon Diggs out, Jayden Daniels will play | Hogs Haven Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Washington Commanders Community Hogs Haven October 16, 2026 Hogs Haven Notifications Notifications Sections News Star Commanders receiver Terry McLaurin was considered questionable to play the Giants on the team’s injury report Commanders receiver Stefon Diggs (hamstring) has been ruled out of Sunday’s game against the New York Giants, head coach Dan Quinn said in his Friday press conference . That’s a big blow, considering Diggs has been Washington’s leading receiver to this point. The Commanders formally listed McLaurin as questionable Friday afternoon on the team’s official injury report. The veteran suffered a hamstring injury in the last practice before Washington played the Colts in London, which kept him from playing that Week 4 game . The Commanders also ruled safety Nick Cross (illness) out after not receiving a medical clearance to play. Adding to that trouble, safeties Percy Butler (hamstring) and Tyler Owens (hamstring) are out of this game. Down three active safeties, Washington must elevate one to get through the game — they just added Darren Hall to the practice squad — where Quan Martin and Jeremy Reaves will play a ton. Defensive end Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle) is also out, which is a big blow to the defensive front. He has been integral to some generally solid run defense. Quarterback Marcus Mariota was ruled out earlier, so that was no shock. The Commanders opened 21-day practice windows for cornerback Trey Amos, defensive lineman Deatrich Wise and running back Jeremy McNichols and designated them questionable — that’s fairly common — but would have to add them to the active roster before playing. Commanders return man and receiver has been lost for the season due to an ankle injury suffered vs. the Colts Notifications Washington Commanders Injuries Fingers are crossed for better news on Terry McLaurin , who was able to practice on Friday and for the first time this week. away.blurb: In fact, Big Blue might be the healthier team on Sunday. The Washington Commanders are dealing with a long list of injuries, even with Jayden Daniels likely set to return to the field. His teammates, on the other hand, have not had such an encouraging week. His top two receivers, Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs, did not participate in practice on Wednesday or Thursday. McLaurin participated in a limited capacity on Friday, but Diggs did not. Both wideouts are dealing with hamstring injuries. If McLaurin and Diggs are both out, Washington will be left with Dyami Brown, Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, and Luke McCaffrey as its only healthy receivers. Commanders' injury report gives Giants a leg up in Week 5, even with Jayden Daniels Skip to main content News It may feel like the New York Giants are the most injured team in the NFL. They are not. Losing Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns, among others, for the season was a devastating blow, but the G-Men still have enough healthy talent on both sides of the ball to remain competitive, especially in a wide-open NFC East. With key commanders missing from the lineup, the Giants have an important advantage in what has become a crucial game in the NFC East title race. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs headline Commanders' injury report vs. Giants Daniels was a full participant in Commanders practice on both Wednesday and Thursday. Barring an unexpected change over the weekend, he should be able to play for the first time since injuring his elbow in Week 2. Of course, the Giants have some important injuries of their own. Braxton Berrios is now set to miss the season with a foot injury. Chauncey Golston's neck injury could leave New York thin on the edge, and safety Jason Pinnock is dealing with a concussion. But in terms of new names popping up on the injury report, the Giants certainly have the advantage in this game. Commanders' injury report gives Giants a clear advantage in Week 5 The Giants' secondary hasn't been stellar this season. The pass defense has been average in most categories and has been torn apart by the most efficient passing offenses it has faced. But if Washington is without its top two wide receivers, New York's secondary should be able to take control of the game. Deonte Banks, who has been a full participant in practice this week , and Greg Newsome II can lock Brown and Burks down on the outside while Dru Phillips handles Williams in the slot. If the Giants limit the Commanders' rushing attack, which hasn't been particularly efficient this year, they can put this game away early.

By Michael Gallagher Sports Content Coordinator 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. The San Francisco 49ers have had arguably the worst injury luck of any team in the NFL this season. More than 15 players are currently on the reserve/injured list while a handful of others are expected to miss some time with their respective ailments. San Francisco’s defense has been hit particularly hard, and star edge-rusher Nick Bosa’s absence over the last few weeks has been noticeable. Keion White has done his part to pick up the slack, but the rest of San Francisco’s pass-rush has left much to be desired, which is why Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report believes the 49ers should make an all-in move to upgrade the position. Knox recently suggested the 49ers execute a trade with the winless Los Angeles Chargers for Pro Bowler Khalil Mack. “Los Angeles fell to 0-5 on Sunday, while Mack continues to be a legitimate difference-maker,” Knox wrote . “… Mack is playing on a one-year deal and should be interested in playing for a team that could get him his first career playoff win. “.. Mack should be the top target for any team with Super Bowl aspirations that happens to need help rushing opposing passers. It'll be a fairly significant surprise if he remains in Los Angeles beyond next month's deadline.” Despite multiple reports indicating the Chargers would want a fifth-round pick in exchange for Mack, Knox suggested it could take at least a conditional 2027 fourth-round pick to get a deal finalized given the demand for strong pass-rushers from contending teams. Through five games this season, Mack has logged 14 pressures, eight hurries, five tackles for loss, three QB hits, and three sacks with a pass-rush win-rate of 9.5%, according to Pro Football Focus. Adding that kind of production opposite White would be a big boost for the 49ers in the interim, and once Bosa comes back, it would make SF’s pass-rush all the more dangerous come playoff time.

home.blurb: While their receiving corps remains banged up with wide receiver Deebo Samuel out multiple weeks with a hamstring injury, head coach Kyle Shanahan on Monday indicated defensive end Nick Bosa (knee, calf), fullback Kyle Juszczyk (knee) and defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. (ankle) all have a chance to return when the 49ers host Washington. Samuel isn't in line to play vs. the Commanders after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 6, but how long he'll be out remains a mystery. Shanahan indicated there's hope Samuel returns after the Week 8 Bye, but he also said the team isn't ruling out an IR stint . Tepid optimism about Nick Bosa return for Week 6 Shanahan on Monday said there was a chance Bosa would be able to play against the Commanders. He didn't rule it out Thursday, but his optimism didn't increase since he last spoke to reporters. Shanahan's pre-practice injury updates Thursday came with some dreadful news about the 49ers' veteran wide receiver. Evans will be out of Thursday's practice, the first of the week, with an Achilles issue Shanahan described as "Achilles soreness." Given Evans' injury history, this one will be worth monitoring very closely throughout the week. Playing through a rib injury is much different than playing through an Achilles issue. Shanahan on Sunday after the 49ers' win over the Seahawks was mum on a Kirk return. The veteran WR is dealing with a calf injury he suffered early in training camp. The 49ers on Thursday announced Kirk's practice window is open, giving the receiver a chance to return for Week 6 where he could help their ailing WR room. WR Deebo Samuel out for multiple weeks The San Francisco 49ers may be getting some injury luck on their side heading into a Week 6 matchup vs. the Washington Commanders . A Monday night game means the 49ers' practice week gets pushed back a day, so the typical Wednesday practice is moved to Thursday. The typical Thursday practice is moved to Friday, and then we'll get an official injury report Saturday.
